In Lemma~\ref{lemma:combin_err}: $i\in[n]$ and $\hat{\mu}_i$ is a measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$ entering the comparison mixture $\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\hat{\mu}_i$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:product_err}: $i\in[n]$ and $\hat{\mu}_i$ is the $i$th factor of $\hat{\mu}=\hat{\mu}_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\hat{\mu}_n$, on the same factor space as $\mu_i$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: $i\in[N_C]$ and $\hat{\mu}_i=P(\hat{g}_2^i\circ\hat{g}_1^i(U_i))$, where $U_i$ is uniform on $[0,1]$; this is the law of the two deterministic component blocks before the Gumbel mixing layer. For $d_i^C=0$, it is the point mass at the singleton $C_i$.
- $X^\tau$: $X^\tau$ uses positive weights $p_1,\ldots,p_n$, which need not sum to one, and $0<\tau<1$, with coordinates indexed by $k\in[n]$; all coordinates are positive and sum to one. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the mixing construction, $n=N_C$ and $p_i=\mathbb{P}(C_i)>0$ for $i\in[N_C]$; $X^\tau$ is the vector of Gumbel-softmax weights assigned to these support components.
- $\tau$: $\tau>0$ is the Gumbel-softmax temperature hyperparameter; a superscript $0$ on a softmax output or layer denotes the limit as $\tau\rightarrow0$, rather than evaluation of the positive-temperature formula at zero. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:gumbel_err}: The temperature satisfies $0<\tau<1$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: The error estimate is asymptotic as the network budgets tend to infinity and $\tau\downarrow0$, with constants independent of the budgets and $\tau$; the proof uses the Gumbel-softmax estimate for $0<\tau<1$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: The temperature is the positive sequence $\tau_n$ appearing in $\mathcal{F}_{1,n}$, with $\tau_n\rightarrow0$. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: The error estimate is asymptotic as the network budgets tend to infinity and $\tau\downarrow0$, with constants independent of the budgets and $\tau$; the proof uses the Gumbel-softmax estimate for $0<\tau<1$. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: The generator temperature is the positive sequence $\tau_n$ in $\mathcal F_{1,n}$ and in the approximation term $\tau_n(1-\log\tau_n)$. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: The displayed error bound is asymptotic as $L_0,L_1,L_2\to\infty$ and $\tau\downarrow0$, with $R>0$ and the causal model fixed. The implicit constant is independent of the intervention and the network budgets, but may depend on $R$ and the fixed causal model.
- $X^0$: $X^0=\lim_{\tau\downarrow0}X^\tau=e_I$ almost surely, where $I=\arg\max_{k\in[n]}(\log p_k+G_k)$, using the same Gumbel draws throughout the limit; ties may be assigned to the first maximizing coordinate. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the mixing construction, $n=N_C$ and $p_i=\mathbb{P}(C_i)>0$ for $i\in[N_C]$; $X^0$ is the one-hot limit of these component weights, with $P(X^0=e_i)=\mathbb{P}(C_i)$.
- $\mu^0$: $\mu^0$ is the law of the one-hot vector $X^0$, supported on the vertices of $\Delta_n$, with $\mu^0(\{e_k\})=p_k/\sum_{j=1}^n p_j$ for $k\in[n]$.
- $n$: $n$ is a local integer parameter whose role is determined by the indexed objects in the surrounding passage. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:hilbert}, Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}: In the partition notation $\mathcal{C}_n$ and the curve and refinement sequences, $n$ is a level index beginning at $0$, with $\mathcal{C}_0=\{C_{-1}\}$ and $C_{-1}=[0,1]^d$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:combin_err}: $n\geqslant1$ is the number of mixture components, with component indices $k=1,\cdots,n$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:product_err}: $n\geqslant1$ is the number of factors in the product measures. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:gumbel_err}: $n\geqslant1$ is the dimension of $X^\tau$ and the number of positive weights $p_k$ and Gumbel coordinates $G_k$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: $n\in\mathbb{N}$ indexes the nested sets, constraint functions, tolerances, and optimization values, and varies in the limit $n\rightarrow\infty$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}: In the local cube-metric definition $C=\prod_{i=1}^{n}[a_i,b_i]$ and $C_k=\prod_{i=1}^{n}[a_i^k,b_i^k]$, $n$ is the ambient dimension and $i$ ranges from $1$ to $n$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sinkhorn_approx}: $n\geqslant1$ is the length of the probability vector $\mu\in\Delta_n$, and a transportation plan has $n$ rows and $m$ columns. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $n$ is the number of observations from the true distribution and also indexes the approximation and tolerance sequences; the asymptotic limit is $n\rightarrow\infty$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $n\geqslant1$ is the sample size defining $\mu_n$ and the number of evaluation points in the empirical covering-number notation $\mathcal{N}_1(\epsilon,\mathcal{F},n)$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: For a component of positive dimension $q=d_i^C$, the refinement integer is $n=\lfloor(W_1/A_q)^{1/q}\rfloor\geqslant2$ for $W_1\geqslant A_q2^q$, where $A_q\geqslant1$ depends only on $q$ and bounds the clipped network width by $A_qn^q$; the quantization parameter is $\delta=1/\lceil\sqrt q(q+1)n(n-1)\rceil$ and the mesh is $\delta/n$. In \cite[Theorem VIII.1]{perekrestenkoHighDimensionalDistributionGeneration2022a}, used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: For a component of positive dimension $q=d_i^C$, the refinement integer is $n=\lfloor(W_1/A_q)^{1/q}\rfloor\geqslant2$ for $W_1\geqslant A_q2^q$, where $A_q\geqslant1$ depends only on $q$ and bounds the clipped network width by $A_qn^q$; the quantization parameter is $\delta=1/\lceil\sqrt q(q+1)n(n-1)\rceil$ and the mesh is $\delta/n$.
- $\mu_n$: $\mu_n$ denotes the locally specified measure, with $n$ serving either as a component index or as the empirical sample size. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:combin_err}: $\mu_n$ is the component measure with index $n$ in the mixture, among measures $\mu_k$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $k\in[n]$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:product_err}: $\mu_n$ is the final component measure in the product $\mu=\mu_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mu_n$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $\mu_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{X_i}$ is the empirical distribution of the sample with law $\mu$, on $\mathbb{R}^{d'}$.
- $W$: The notation $W(\mu,\nu)$ denotes Wasserstein-1 distance between measures on the same underlying space, whereas $W$ in a network architecture argument denotes an integer width. In \cite[Theorem 2]{Yarotsky2018OptimalAO}, used in the proof of Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: In $a\,\omega(cW^{-2/d_i^{\text{in}}})$, $W$ is the number of weights of the scalar approximating network, rather than its width; at fixed width $2d_i^{\text{in}}+10$, this weight count grows linearly in the depth $L_0$.
- $\lambda$: $\lambda$ is a positive scalar when it indexes a regularized transport functional and a reference measure when it occurs in a push-forward or measure-domination expression, with its reference domain specified locally. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the push-forward expression, $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]^{N_C}$; in the componentwise construction, it is the uniform measure on $[0,1]$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}: For the curve's push-forward, $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$; in expressions $\lambda(B)$ with $B\subset[0,1]^d$, it is $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sinkhorn_approx}: $\lambda>0$ is the scalar regularization parameter. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the push-forward expression, $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]^{N_C}$; in the componentwise construction, it is the uniform measure on $[0,1]$, and in the lower-bound premise it is Lebesgue measure on the corresponding cube.
- $S_\lambda$: $S_\lambda$ is the debiased regularized transport functional obtained by subtracting half of each self-comparison from $W_{1,\lambda}(\mu,\nu)$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sinkhorn_approx}: The arguments are finite probability measures represented by their weights and support points, with $c_{ij}=\|x_i-y_j\|$ for the $1$-norm. Here $W_{1,\lambda}(\mu,\nu)=\min_{T\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\{\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}T_{ij}-\lambda h(T)\}$, where $\Pi(\mu,\nu)$ is the set of nonnegative transportation plans with marginals $\mu,\nu$, and $h(T)=1-\sum_{i,j}T_{ij}\log T_{ij}$ with $0\log0=0$. Both self terms use this same convention and the same $1$-norm ground distance on their corresponding support points.
- $W_{1,\lambda}$: $W_{1,\lambda}$ uses the supplied finite support points, the paper's $1$-norm ground cost, and the entropy subtraction $-\lambda h(T)$ with $h(T)=1-\sum_{i,j}T_{ij}\log T_{ij}$ and $0\log0=0$.
- $L$: $L$ denotes a nonnegative Lipschitz bound with respect to the paper's $1$-norm when used in a Lipschitz condition or $\mathcal{F}_L$, and an integer depth when used as the depth argument of a neural network class. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}, Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}, Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}: In the SCM class $\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{F}_L,\boldsymbol{U})$, $L$ bounds the continuous structural functions and the categorical propensity functions, rather than the categorical $\arg\max$ maps. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:push-forward_err}: $L$ is a Lipschitz bound for $F$; the hypothesis does not impose that bound on $\hat{F}$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:Lip_condition}: $L$ is a common Lipschitz bound for the regression functions $f$ and $\hat{f}$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}, Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the support assumptions, $L$ bounds the homeomorphisms from the unit cubes to the support sets; it is not a Lipschitz bound for the resulting space-filling curves. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In $\mathcal F_L^K$ and $\underline F^L$, $L$ bounds the Lipschitz constants of the continuous structural functions and normalized categorical propensity vectors of population candidate SCMs, with respect to the paper's $1$-norm; the class also requires $\sup_x\|f(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ on the full structural input domain. The conclusion evaluates this parameter at $\hat L_f$. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the support assumptions, $L$ bounds the homeomorphisms from the unit cubes to the support sets; it is not a Lipschitz bound for the resulting space-filling curves.
- $\mathcal{F}_L$: $\mathcal{F}_L(K_1,K_2)$ denotes the class of maps $f:K_1\rightarrow K_2$ with Lipschitz constant at most $L$, using the paper's $1$-norm convention, with the arguments supplied by context when omitted.
- $\mathcal{H}$: $\mathcal{H}(K_1,K_2)$ denotes homeomorphisms from $K_1$ onto $K_2$, while an explicit local definition of unparameterized $\mathcal{H}$ supplies its function class. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: In the proof, $\mathcal{H}=\left\{h:h\in\mathcal{F}_1([-K,K]^d,[-K,K]^d),\ h(0)=0\right\}$, and $\mathcal{H}_\delta$ is a $\delta$-net of this class in the $\ell_\infty$ norm.
- $\mathcal{F}$: $\mathcal{F}$ denotes a function class whose domains and codomains are supplied by its local use. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}, Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}, Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample_foral}, Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample}, Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}, Proposition~\ref{prop:equivalent_g_constrianed}: In $\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{F},\boldsymbol{U})$, $\mathcal{F}$ specifies the allowed structural functions, with $f_i\in\mathcal{F}$ for $i\in[n_V]$; each function has the input and output dimensions of its structural equation. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $\mathcal F$ is a class of measurable maps $f:\mathbb R^{d'}\rightarrow\mathbb R^d$. Each scalar coordinate class $\mathcal F_j=\{x\mapsto f_j(x):f\in\mathcal F\}$, $j\in[d]$, has pseudo-dimension less than $d_{\mathcal F}<\infty$, and $\|f(x)\|_\infty\leqslant K$ for every $f\in\mathcal F$ and $x\in\mathbb R^{d'}$. There are a standard Borel space $T$ and a jointly Borel map $G:T\times\mathbb R^{d'}\rightarrow[-K,K]^d$ such that $\mathcal F=\{G(t,\cdot):t\in T\}$.
- $K$: $K$ is a context-dependent bound or compact set: numerical occurrences are positive bounds, whereas set-valued occurrences specify the compact domain or support of a measure. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}, Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}, Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample_foral}, Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample}, Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: In the boundedness assumption, $K>0$ satisfies $\max_{i\in[n_V],j\in[n_U]}\{\|V_i\|_\infty,\|U_j\|_\infty\}\leqslant K$; the indexed $U_j$ are the latent variables separated from the categorical Gumbel noises. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:push-forward_err}: $K\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_1}$ is the compact set carrying $\mu$ and $\hat{\mu}$ and the common domain of $F$ and $\hat{F}$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:Lip_condition}: $K$ bounds the regression functions: $|f(t)|\leqslant K$ and $|\hat{f}(t)|\leqslant K$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}, Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}, Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample_foral}, Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample}, Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the lower-bound support assumption, $K\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}$ is compact and supports the measure under consideration; $f\in\mathcal{H}([0,1]^d,K)\cap\mathcal{F}_L([0,1]^d,K)$. This set-valued occurrence is distinct from a numerical boundedness constant. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the explanatory notation $\mathcal{P}(K)$, $K$ is the set on which probability measures are defined; in the displayed factors $\mathcal{P}([-K,K]^{d_j^U})$, the $K$ inside the cube endpoints is the numerical boundedness constant. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: In the truncated neural classes, numerical $K$ is the clipping level in $\max\{-K,\min\{f,K\}\}$ and is the boundedness constant chosen for the underlying SCM. Every true continuous structural function and every candidate continuous structural network additionally satisfies $\sup_x\|f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ and $\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$, respectively, on its full structural input domain. The limiting structural class retains $\mathcal F_L^K=\{f:\sup_x\|f(x)\|_1\leqslant K,\ \operatorname{Lip}(f)\leqslant L\}$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $K>0$ is the uniform output bound $\|f(x)\|_\infty\leqslant K$ for every $f\in\mathcal F$ and every $x\in\mathbb R^{d'}$; consequently the outputs lie in $[-K,K]^d$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample_foral}: For each non-Gumbel latent law $\mathbb P$ with support components $C_i$, Assumption~\ref{assumption:lower_bound} applies to every normalized component law $\mu_i=\mathbb P|_{C_i}/\mathbb P(C_i)$ with the compact support set $K=C_i$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample}: For each non-Gumbel latent law $\mathbb P$ with support components $C_i$, Assumption~\ref{assumption:lower_bound} applies to every normalized component law $\mu_i=\mathbb P|_{C_i}/\mathbb P(C_i)$ with the compact support set $K=C_i$. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: For each non-Gumbel latent law $\mathbb P=P(U_C)$ with support components $C_i$, the lower-bound support assumption applies to each normalized component law $\mu_i=\mathbb P|_{C_i}/\mathbb P(C_i)$ with compact support set $K=C_i$. Its chart $f:[0,1]^{d_i^C}\rightarrow C_i$ satisfies $(f^{-1})_{\#}\mu_i(\partial[0,1]^{d_i^C})=0$ when $d_i^C>0$.
- $\mathcal{F}_L^K$: $\mathcal{F}_L^K(K_1,K_2)$ denotes a class of bounded Lipschitz continuous maps $f:K_1\rightarrow K_2$, with the norm bound and Lipschitz restriction given by its local definition. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the statement and the limiting optimization, $\mathcal F_L^K=\{f:\sup_x\|f(x)\|_1\leqslant K,\ \operatorname{Lip}(f)\leqslant L\}$, with the supremum over the full structural input domain; in the proof's displayed population-function definition, $\mathcal F_L^K=\{f:\|f\|_\infty\leqslant K,\ f\ \text{Lipschitz continuous}\}$, where the function infinity norm is the uniform coordinatewise bound and that display supplies no numerical Lipschitz bound. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: The population bounded Lipschitz class is $\mathcal F_L^K=\{f:\sup_x\|f(x)\|_1\leqslant K,\ \operatorname{Lip}(f)\leqslant L\}$, with the supremum over the full structural input domain.
- $\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{F},\boldsymbol{U})$: $\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{F},\boldsymbol{U})$ consists of canonical SCMs on $\mathcal{G}$ with $f_i\in\mathcal{F}$ for $i\in[n_V]$ and the indicated canonical latent coordinates; the argument $\boldsymbol{U}$ does not fix a common latent probability law across the class.
- $\mathcal{NN}$: The two-argument notation $\mathcal{NN}_{k_1,k_2}(W,L)$ specifies a ReLU network class, with omitted dimensions supplied by context; the five-argument notation specifies the separable three-part generator architecture including its Gumbel-Softmax layer. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: The four-argument generator class $\mathcal{NN}(\Theta(d_{\max}^U),L_1,\Theta((d_{\max}^U)^2),L_2)$ suppresses the temperature $\tau$ of the same third Gumbel-Softmax layer, which remains present in the approximation bound. The multiplicative width factors in $\Theta(d_{\max}^{\text{in}}d_{\max}^{\text{out}})$, $\Theta(d_{\max}^U)$, and $\Theta((d_{\max}^U)^2)$ can be chosen as absolute numerical constants, independent of the causal model, $R$, all dimensions, and all category and component counts. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the generator architecture, a component with $d_i^C=0$ uses the unique map to $[0,1]^0$ as its first deterministic block and a constant affine map to its singleton support component as its second deterministic block. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: The multiplicative width factors in $\Theta(D_C)$ and $\Theta(dD_C)$ are absolute numerical constants, independent of the measure, chart constants, dimensions, and component count.
- $\mathcal{NN}(W_1,L_1,W_2,L_2,\tau)$: This is the three-part generator class with component count $N_C$, component cube dimensions $d_j^C$, and output dimension $d$ suppressed from its arguments; $W_1,L_1$ and $W_2,L_2$ specify the respective component-network widths and depths, and $\tau>0$ specifies the mixing temperature. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: The four-argument generator-class occurrence suppresses the temperature argument; the latent generators retain the Gumbel-softmax temperature $\tau$ appearing in the bound. The multiplicative width factors in $\Theta(d_{\max}^U)$ and $\Theta((d_{\max}^U)^2)$ can be chosen as absolute numerical constants, independent of the causal model, $R$, all dimensions, and all category and component counts. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: The class used is its truncated version $\mathcal{NN}^{\infty,K}(\Theta(d_{\max}^U),L_{1,n},\Theta((d_{\max}^U)^2),L_{2,n},\tau_n)$; the superscript $\infty$ imposes no finite Lipschitz bound, while $K$ specifies coordinatewise output truncation, and the finite component counts and component cube dimensions of the latent generator architectures are fixed as $n$ varies. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: The architecture includes components with $d_i^C=0$: their first deterministic block is the unique map to $[0,1]^0$, and their second deterministic block is a constant affine map to the corresponding singleton. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: The latent generator class is the truncated class $\mathcal F_{1,n}=\mathcal{NN}^{\infty,K}(\Theta(d_{\max}^U),L_{1,n},\Theta((d_{\max}^U)^2),L_{2,n},\tau_n)$; the superscript $\infty$ imposes no finite Lipschitz bound, $K$ specifies coordinatewise output truncation, and the finite component counts and component cube dimensions are fixed as $n$ varies. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: The multiplicative width factors in $\Theta(D_C)$ and $\Theta(dD_C)$ are absolute numerical constants, independent of the measure, chart constants, dimensions, and component count.
- $\mathcal{NN}^{L_f,K}$: $\mathcal{NN}^{L_f,K}(W,L)$ abbreviates $\mathcal{NN}_{d_1,d_2}^{L_f,K}(W,L)=\{\max\{-K,\min\{f,K\}\}:f\in\mathcal{NN}_{d_1,d_2}(W,L),\ \text{Lip}(f)\leqslant L_f\}$, with coordinatewise clipping and dimensions supplied by the function being represented; here $L$ is network depth. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: The ambient structural class is $\mathcal F_{0,n}=\mathcal{NN}^{\hat L_f,K}(W_{0,n},\Theta(\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}}))$, where the depth expression uses $\Theta(1+\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}})$ when $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}=1$; categorical raw structural members $q$ admitted to the empirical optimization additionally satisfy $q(x)\in[0,\infty)^{n_i}$, $\|q(x)\|_1>0$ for every structural input $x$, and $\operatorname{Lip}(x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1)\leqslant\hat L_f$, while each admitted continuous structural network $\hat f_i$ additionally satisfies $\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ on its full structural input domain. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: The ambient structural class is $\mathcal F_{0,n}=\mathcal{NN}^{\hat L_f,K}(W_{0,n},\Theta(\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}}))$, with the depth convention inherited from its specification; each categorical raw structural network $q$ admitted to the empirical optimization additionally satisfies $q(x)\in[0,\infty)^{n_i}$, $\|q(x)\|_1>0$ for every structural input $x$, and $\operatorname{Lip}(x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1)\leqslant\hat L_f$, while each admitted continuous structural network $\hat f_i$ additionally satisfies $\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ on its full structural input domain.
- $W_1$: $W_1$ is the integer width of each component network $\hat{g}_1^j\in\mathcal{NN}_{1,d_j^C}(W_1,L_1)$, $j\in[N_C]$, rather than the combined width of all parallel component networks. In \cite[Theorem VIII.1]{perekrestenkoHighDimensionalDistributionGeneration2022a}, used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: For each component of positive dimension $q=d_i^C$, the construction takes $W_1\geqslant A_q2^q$ and $n=\lfloor(W_1/A_q)^{1/q}\rfloor$, where $A_q\geqslant1$ depends only on $q$ and bounds the clipped network width by $A_qn^q$.
- $W_2$: $W_2$ is the integer width of each component network $\hat{g}_2^j\in\mathcal{NN}_{d_j^C,d}(W_2,L_2)$, $j\in[N_C]$.
- $L_1$: $L_1$ is the integer depth of each component network $\hat{g}_1^j\in\mathcal{NN}_{1,d_j^C}(W_1,L_1)$, $j\in[N_C]$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: At sample size $n$, the first-block depth is $L_{1,n}$, with $L_{1,n}=\Theta(m_n^{d_{\max}^U/(2d_{\max}^U+4)})$; the architectural order uses sufficiently large fixed constant factors supplied by the network constructions. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: The displayed error bound is asymptotic as $L_0,L_1,L_2\to\infty$ and $\tau\downarrow0$, with $R$ and the causal model fixed; $R>0$ is fixed before choosing $\hat{\mathcal M}$. The implicit constant is independent of the intervention and the network budgets, but may depend on $R$ and the fixed causal model.
- $L_2$: $L_2$ is the integer depth of each component network $\hat{g}_2^j\in\mathcal{NN}_{d_j^C,d}(W_2,L_2)$, $j\in[N_C]$. In \cite[Theorem 2]{Yarotsky2018OptimalAO}, used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: $L_2$ is also the depth of each scalar coordinate approximant $\hat{g}_2^{i,j}$ used to form $\hat{g}_2^i=(\hat{g}_2^{i,1},\ldots,\hat{g}_2^{i,d})$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: At sample size $n$, the second-block depth is $L_{2,n}$, with $L_{2,n}=\Theta(m_n^{d_{\max}^U/(2d_{\max}^U+4)})$; the architectural order uses sufficiently large fixed constant factors supplied by the network constructions. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: The displayed error bound is asymptotic as $L_0,L_1,L_2\to\infty$ and $\tau\downarrow0$, with $R$ and the causal model fixed; $R>0$ is fixed before choosing $\hat{\mathcal M}$. The implicit constant is independent of the intervention and the network budgets, but may depend on $R$ and the fixed causal model.
- $\mathcal{NN}^{\infty,K}$: $\mathcal{NN}^{\infty,K}$ clips the final generator output coordinatewise to $[-K,K]$, with no imposed Lipschitz bound; its suppressed dimensions and component structure are those of the corresponding generator class.
- $\hat{g}$: The notation $\hat{g}_{\#}\lambda$ denotes the output law of the generator after integrating both its uniform input and its Gumbel-softmax randomness, rather than a push-forward conditional on a realized mixing vector. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: The generator has uniform-input dimension $N_C$, output dimension $d$, and target law $\mathbb{P}$; its mixing weights are the target component masses. A component with $d_i^C=0$ is a singleton, and its two deterministic blocks are the unique map to $[0,1]^0$ and a constant affine map to that singleton. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}, Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the NCM class notation, $\hat{g}\in\mathcal{F}_1$ is shorthand for the separate latent generators $\hat{g}_j$, whose compatible dimensions depend on the corresponding latent variable. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: At sample size $n$, generators range over $\mathcal{F}_{1,n}$ and have coordinatewise output truncation to $[-K,K]$, with finite component counts and component cube dimensions fixed as $n$ varies. The optimization ranges over network representations, including distinct representations inducing the same latent population laws; each representation is evaluated on the same $m_n$ exogenous input draws. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: The generator has uniform-input dimension $N_C$, output dimension $d$, and target law $\mathbb{P}$; its mixing weights are the target component masses. A component with $d_i^C=0$ is a singleton, and its two deterministic blocks are the unique map to $[0,1]^0$ and a constant affine map to that singleton.
- $\text{NCM}_{\mathcal{G}}$: $\text{NCM}_{\mathcal{G}}(\mathcal{F}_0,\mathcal{F}_1)$ is the collection of models on $\mathcal{G}$ with structural equations (\ref{eq:structure_equation_hat}), in which every structural network belongs to $\mathcal{F}_0$ and every component-specific latent generator belongs to $\mathcal{F}_1$, with compatible dimensions suppressed. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: At sample size $n$, the candidate class is $\text{NCM}_{\mathcal G}(\mathcal F_{0,n},\mathcal F_{1,n})$, with the architecture and truncation specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, restricted so that every categorical raw structural network $q$ satisfies $q(x)\in[0,\infty)^{n_i}$, $\|q(x)\|_1>0$ for every structural input $x$, and $\operatorname{Lip}(x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1)\leqslant\hat L_f$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: The empirical optimization ranges over network representations in the restricted candidate class; representations with the same latent population laws remain distinct candidates and may yield different common-draw empirical distributions. Every admitted continuous structural network additionally satisfies $\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ on its full structural input domain. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: Candidates are evaluated as network representations on the same $m_n$ exogenous simulation draws; representations with identical latent population laws can yield different empirical distributions on these common draws. Every admitted continuous structural network additionally satisfies $\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ on its full structural input domain.
- $\mathcal{F}_0$: $\mathcal{F}_0$ is the structural-network class supplied to $\text{NCM}_{\mathcal{G}}(\mathcal{F}_0,\mathcal{F}_1)$, with the input and output dimensions appropriate to each node omitted from the notation. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: The class is $\mathcal{F}_{0,n}=\mathcal{NN}^{\hat L_f,K}(W_{0,n},\Theta(\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}}))$, where $\hat L_f=\sqrt{d_{\max}^{\text{in}}d_{\max}^{\text{out}}}L_f$; it consists of coordinatewise truncations to $[-K,K]$ of networks whose Lipschitz constant is at most $\hat L_f$, and varies with $n$. When $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}=1$, the depth expression uses $\Theta(1+\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}})$. Continuous structural networks admitted to the optimization additionally satisfy $\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ on their full structural input domains. Categorical raw networks admitted to the optimization additionally satisfy $q(x)\in[0,\infty)^{n_i}$, $\|q(x)\|_1>0$ for every structural input $x$, and $\operatorname{Lip}(x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1)\leqslant\hat L_f$.
- $\mathcal{F}_1$: $\mathcal{F}_1$ is function-class notation whose subscript can be a class identifier or the Lipschitz constant in the previously defined notation $\mathcal{F}_L(K_1,K_2)$. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}, Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: As the second argument of $\text{NCM}_{\mathcal{G}}(\mathcal{F}_0,\mathcal{F}_1)$, the class restricts the latent generators, with input and output dimensions omitted from the notation. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: The latent-generator class is $\mathcal{F}_{1,n}=\mathcal{NN}^{\infty,K}(\Theta(d_{\max}^U),L_{1,n},\Theta((d_{\max}^U)^2),L_{2,n},\tau_n)$, a class varying with $n$.
- $\hat{g}_1$: Each coordinate block $\hat{g}_1^j$ uses one scalar input to generate coordinates in the cube $[0,1]^{d_j^C}$ associated with component $j$, without mixing inputs from different components. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: Writing $\mu_j=\mathbb{P}_{C_j}/\mathbb{P}(C_j)$, for $d_j^C\geqslant1$ the first block approximates the cube law $((g_2^j)^{-1})_{\#}\mu_j$ by the law of $\hat{g}_1^j(U_j)$; for $d_j^C=0$, it is the unique map to $[0,1]^0$.
- $\hat{g}_2$: Each coordinate block $\hat{g}_2^j$ maps the $d_j^C$-dimensional cube coordinates for component $j$ into $\mathbb{R}^d$, without mixing inputs from different components. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: For $d_j^C\geqslant1$, the block $\hat{g}_2^j$ approximates a map $g_2^j\in\mathcal{H}([0,1]^{d_j^C},C_j)\cap\mathcal{F}_L([0,1]^{d_j^C},C_j)$; for $d_j^C=0$, it is a constant affine map to the singleton $C_j$.
- $\hat{g}_3^\tau$: $\hat{g}_3^\tau$ mixes the $N_C$ component outputs using the Gumbel-softmax coefficient vector, with $\tau>0$; the notation $\hat{g}_3^0$ denotes its almost-sure hard-selection limit as $\tau\rightarrow0$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: The mixing weights are $p_k=\mathbb{P}(C_k)$ for the connected components $C_k$ of the target support. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: The layer is used separately for each latent generator, with mixing weights given by the masses of the connected components of that latent variable's target law. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: At sample size $n$, the generator class uses temperature $\tau_n>0$ and truncates the resulting generator output coordinatewise to $[-K,K]$. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: The mixing weights are $p_k=\mathbb{P}(C_k)$ for the connected components $C_k$ of the target support.
- $g_2^i$: For $i\in[N_C]$, $g_2^i$ is a chosen map in $\mathcal{H}([0,1]^{d_i^C},C_i)\cap\mathcal{F}_L([0,1]^{d_i^C},C_i)$, whose inverse pulls the component law back to the unit cube. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: $g_2^i$ is chosen so that $(g_2^i)^{-1}_{\#}\mu_i(B)\geqslant C_g\lambda(B)/\mathbb{P}(C_i)$ for every measurable $B\subset[0,1]^{d_i^C}$, where $\mu_i=\mathbb{P}_{C_i}/\mathbb{P}(C_i)$ and $\lambda$ is cube Lebesgue measure. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: For $d_i^C=0$, $g_2^i$ is the unique map from $[0,1]^0$ to the singleton $C_i$.
- $\hat{g}_2^{i,j}$: For $i\in[N_C]$ and $j\in[d]$, $\hat{g}_2^{i,j}:[0,1]^{d_i^C}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ denotes a coordinate network chosen to approximate $(g_2^i)_j$ uniformly on $[0,1]^{d_i^C}$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: When $d_i^C=0$, $\hat{g}_2^{i,j}$ is the $j$th coordinate of the constant affine map to the singleton $C_i$, so its approximation error is zero.
- $\gamma_i$: For $i\in[N_C]$, $\gamma_i$ represents the pullback of the normalized component law $\mu_i$ through $g_2^i$, wherever $\mathbb{P}(C_i)>0$.
- $\hat{g}_1^{i,j}$: For $i\in[N_C]$ and $j\in[d_i^C]$, $\hat{g}_1^{i,j}:[0,1]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ denotes a coordinate network chosen to approximate $(\gamma_i)_j$ uniformly on $[0,1]$.
- $Z_{C_j}$: $Z_{C_j}$ denotes the uniform and Gumbel input vector for the generator of the latent variable associated with graph $C^2$-component $C_j$, with $N_{C,j}$ uniform coordinates and $N_{C,j}$ Gumbel coordinates, where $N_{C,j}$ counts the connected components of $\operatorname{supp}(P(U_{C_j}))$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: At each sample size $n$, the simulation inputs $Z_{C_j}^{(r)}$, $r\in[m_n]$, are shared across all candidate network representations: each candidate latent generator is evaluated as $\hat g_j(Z_{C_j}^{(r)})$. These inputs are drawn as part of the common independent and identically distributed exogenous product-law draws, independently of the observational sample.
- $\hat{U}_{C_j}$: For a $C^2$-component $C_j$ of $\mathcal{G}$, $\hat{U}_{C_j}=\hat{g}_j(Z_{C_j})$ denotes the generated latent vector corresponding to $U_{C_j}$, with law $(\hat{g}_j)_{\#}P(Z_{C_j})$.
- $N_C$: $N_C$ denotes the finite number of connected components of $\operatorname{supp}(\mathbb P)$, indexed by $i\in[N_C]$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: The finite component count of each latent generator architecture in $\mathcal F_{1,n}$ is fixed as $n$ varies.
- $d_i^C$: For $i\in[N_C]$, $d_i^C$ is a nonnegative integer such that $\mathcal{H}([0,1]^{d_i^C},C_i)\cap\mathcal{F}_L([0,1]^{d_i^C},C_i)\neq\emptyset$; $d_i^C=0$ corresponds to a singleton component. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: The component cube dimensions of each latent generator architecture in $\mathcal F_{1,n}$ are fixed as $n$ varies.
- $C_f$: $C_f$ is a positive domination constant associated with the particular measure $\mathbb{P}$ and chosen homeomorphism $f$ in the lower-bound assumption.
- $\gamma$: $\gamma$ denotes a continuous measure-representing curve parametrized by $[0,1]$, with parameter measure $\lambda$ equal to Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}: In the statement, $\gamma:[0,1]\rightarrow\operatorname{supp}(\mathbb{P})$ satisfies $\gamma_{\#}\lambda=\mathbb{P}$ and is $1/d$-H\"older continuous when $d\geqslant1$. In the proof's change of coordinates, the locally denoted $\gamma$ instead satisfies $\gamma_{\#}\lambda=f^{-1}_{\#}\mathbb{P}$; the curve representing the original measure is $f\circ\gamma$. For $d=0$, the representing curve is constant.
- $\mathcal{C}_n$: For $n\geqslant0$, $\mathcal{C}_0=\{[0,1]^d\}$ and $\mathcal{C}_n=\{C_{i_1,\ldots,i_n}:i_j\in\{0,\ldots,2^d-1\}\}$ is a coordinate-plane partition satisfying property (*), with each cell the union of its $2^d$ children. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}: For $d\geqslant1$, the full cube-coordinate construction recursively refines closed coordinate cells by cuts near their coordinate midpoints, perturbing the cuts to obtain $\mathbb{P}(\partial C)=0$ for each cell. It requires $R(\mathcal{C}_{n+1})\leqslant(1+2^{-n})R(\mathcal{C}_n)$; its cells need not be the standard dyadic cubes. Here $\mathbb{P}$ is the measure after the proof's change to cube coordinates. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:hilbert}: When $d\geqslant1$, $\mathcal{C}_n=\{\prod_{r=1}^d[a_r2^{-n},(a_r+1)2^{-n}]:a_r\in\{0,\ldots,2^n-1\}\}$; these cells are closed and may share boundaries.
- $O_n$: For each positive refinement level $n$, $O_n$ is an ordering, hence a bijection, from $\{1,\ldots,2^{nd}\}$ onto $\{\overline{i_1\cdots i_n}:i_j\in\{0,\ldots,2^d-1\}\}$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:hilbert}: The chosen sequence preserves parent prefixes: the first $n$ digits of $O_{n+1}(i)$ equal $O_n(j)$ when $(j-1)2^d<i\leqslant j2^d$; for $1\leqslant i<2^{nd}$, consecutive cells $C_{O_n(i)}$ and $C_{O_n(i+1)}$ share a $(d-1)$-dimensional face. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}: The proof chooses the sequence $\{O_n\}$ for its recursively constructed cube partitions with parent-prefix consistency: the first $n$ digits of $O_{n+1}(i)$ equal $O_n(j)$ for $(j-1)2^d<i\leqslant j2^d$. Consecutive cells share a $(d-1)$-dimensional face for $1\leqslant i<2^{nd}$, and this ordering determines the order of the corresponding mass-weighted parameter intervals.
- $\mathcal{I}_n$: For $n\geqslant0$, $\mathcal{I}_n$ is the nested collection of closed parameter intervals covering $[0,1]$, ordered by $O_n$ and matched to $\mathcal{C}_n$ with $|I_{O_n(i)}|=\mathbb{P}(C_{O_n(i)})$, where $\mathbb{P}$ is the measure in the cube coordinates of the construction.
- $f_k$: $f_k$ denotes a locally indexed deterministic map whose domain and meaning are those of the surrounding structural-model or partition construction. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}, Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: $f_k$ is the structural function at observed node $V_k$, with inputs its parents and affecting non-Gumbel latent variables; its output is the continuous value or the normalized categorical propensity vector, as appropriate.
- $F_n$: $F_n$ is the scalar infimum of $\mathbb{E}_{t\sim\mu_T}\mathbb{E}_{\hat{\mathcal{M}}}[F(V_1(t),\ldots,V_{n_V}(t))]$ over the candidate neural causal models admitted by the empirical optimization, subject to $S_{\lambda_n}(P_{m_n}^{\hat{\mathcal{M}}}(\boldsymbol{V}),P_n^{\mathcal{M}^*}(\boldsymbol{V}))\leqslant\alpha_n$, wherever this value is defined; an attained minimum has the same value. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $F_n$ is the optimal value of the locally specified restricted optimization, retaining the objective and Sinkhorn constraint of (\ref{eq:opt_empiri}) and using the specified classes $\mathcal F_{0,n}$ and $\mathcal F_{1,n}$. The minimized objective is $\frac{1}{t_2-t_1}\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\mathbb E_{\hat{\mathcal M}}[Y(t)]\,dt$. Each continuous structural network $\hat f_i\in\mathcal F_{0,n}$ satisfies $\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ on its full structural input domain. Each categorical raw structural network $q\in\mathcal F_{0,n}$ satisfies $q(x)\in[0,\infty)^{n_i}$, $\|q(x)\|_1>0$ for every structural input $x$, and $\operatorname{Lip}(x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1)\leqslant\hat L_f$. For each sample size, every candidate empirical law is obtained by evaluating the candidate on the same $m_n$ independent draws of its uniform and Gumbel exogenous inputs, independent of the observational sample. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: The optimization ranges over network representations using $\mathcal F_{0,n}$ and $\mathcal F_{1,n}$. Each continuous structural network $\hat f_i$ satisfies $\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ on its full structural input domain. Each categorical raw structural network $q\in\mathcal F_{0,n}$ satisfies $q(x)\in[0,\infty)^{n_i}$, $\|q(x)\|_1>0$ for every structural input $x$, and $\operatorname{Lip}(x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1)\leqslant\hat L_f$. For each $n$, all candidates are evaluated on the same $m_n$ independent and identically distributed draws of all exogenous inputs according to their specified product law, including uniform inputs, generator Gumbel inputs, and categorical Gumbel inputs, independent of the observational sample; representations with the same latent population laws may yield different empirical constraints.
- $\mu_T$: $\mu_T$ is the given measure on treatment intervention values used in the outer expectation $\mathbb{E}_{t\sim\mu_T}$. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $\mu_T=\operatorname{Unif}([t_1,t_2])$, $\mu_T\ll P$, and $A_T^2=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}(d\mu_T/dP(t))^2P(dt)<\infty$, where $P$ is the reference probability measure on the treatment space.
- $F_*$: $F_*=\mathbb{E}_{t\sim\mu_T}\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{M}^*}[F(V_1(t),\ldots,V_{n_V}(t))]$ denotes the population objective evaluated at the true SCM. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $F_*=\frac{1}{t_2-t_1}\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{M}^*}[Y(t)]\,dt$, since $F(\boldsymbol{V})=Y$ and $\mu_T=\operatorname{Unif}([t_1,t_2])$.
- $\underline{F}^L$: $\underline{F}^L$ is the population optimal objective value in equation~\ref{eq:consistent_limiting}, minimizing $\mathbb{E}_{t\sim\mu_T}\mathbb{E}_{\hat{\mathcal{M}}}[F(V_1(t),\ldots,V_{n_V}(t))]$ over canonical SCMs on $\mathcal{G}$ with structural functions in $\mathcal{F}_L^K$ and all latent distributions $P(\boldsymbol{U})$, subject to $W(P^{\hat{\mathcal{M}}}(\boldsymbol{V}),P^{\mathcal{M}^*}(\boldsymbol{V}))=0$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: $\underline F^L$ uses the class $\mathcal F_L^K=\{f:\sup_x\|f(x)\|_1\leqslant K,\ \operatorname{Lip}(f)\leqslant L\}$ in equation~\ref{eq:consistent_limiting}, with the supremum taken over the full structural input domain; categorical structural functions are normalized propensity vectors. The conclusion evaluates this population optimal value at $L=\hat L_f$.
- $P_n^{\mathcal{M}^*}$: $P_n^{\mathcal{M}^*}(\boldsymbol V)=n^{-1}\sum_{a=1}^n\delta_{\boldsymbol V^{(a)}}$ is the empirical observational law of the $n$ observed joint values from $P^{\mathcal{M}^*}(\boldsymbol V)$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: The $n$ observations defining $P_n^{\mathcal M^*}(\boldsymbol V)$ are independent complete observations with common law $P^{\mathcal M^*}(\boldsymbol V)$.
- $m_n$: $m_n$ is a prescribed positive integer sequence, indexed by the observational sample size $n$, giving the simulation sample size for each candidate model. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: The simulation sizes satisfy $m_n=\Omega(n)$; equality $m_n=n$ is not required.
- $P_{m_n}^{\hat{\mathcal{M}}}$: $P_{m_n}^{\hat{\mathcal{M}}}(\boldsymbol{V})$ denotes the empirical observational law for the candidate $\hat{\mathcal{M}}$, namely $m_n^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^{m_n}\delta_{\boldsymbol{V}^{(r)}}$, and is indexed by the candidate rather than denoting only the law at an optimizer. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: For each $n$, $P_{m_n}^{\hat{\mathcal{M}}}(\boldsymbol{V})$ is obtained by evaluating every candidate network representation on the same $m_n$ independent draws of all exogenous inputs, including uniform inputs, generator Gumbel inputs, and categorical Gumbel inputs; these draws are independent of the observational sample. Different network representations with the same latent population laws may give different common-draw empirical distributions. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: For each $n$, $P_{m_n}^{\hat{\mathcal{M}}}(\boldsymbol{V})$ is obtained by evaluating every candidate network representation on the same $m_n$ independent draws of all exogenous inputs, including uniform inputs, generator Gumbel inputs, and categorical Gumbel inputs; these draws are independent of the observational sample. Different network representations with the same latent population laws may give different common-draw empirical distributions.
- $\mathcal{F}_{0,n}$: $\mathcal{F}_{0,n}$ is the prescribed structural network class at sample size $n$, with the input and output dimensions appropriate to the node and with truncation applied coordinatewise. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the parameter-space construction, a continuous-node candidate is a function $\hat f_i\in\mathcal{F}_{0,n}$ satisfying $\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ on its full structural input domain. A categorical-node propensity is represented by $x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1$ with $q\in\mathcal{F}_{0,n}$ restricted to satisfy $q(x)\in[0,\infty)^{n_i}$ and $\|q(x)\|_1>0$ for every structural input $x$, and $\operatorname{Lip}(x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1)\leqslant\hat L_f$. The depth expression $\Theta(\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}})$ uses $\Theta(1+\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}})$ when $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}=1$. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: A continuous-node candidate is a function $\hat f_i\in\mathcal{F}_{0,n}$ satisfying $\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ on its full structural input domain. A categorical-node propensity is represented by $x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1$ with $q\in\mathcal{F}_{0,n}$ restricted to satisfy $q(x)\in[0,\infty)^{n_i}$ and $\|q(x)\|_1>0$ for every structural input $x$, and $\operatorname{Lip}(x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1)\leqslant\hat L_f$. The depth expression $\Theta(\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}})$ uses $\Theta(1+\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}})$ when $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}=1$.
- $\mathcal{F}_{1,n}$: $\mathcal{F}_{1,n}$ is the latent-generator network class indexed by $n$, with architecture $\mathcal{NN}^{\infty,K}(\Theta(d_{\max}^{U}),L_{1,n},\Theta((d_{\max}^{U})^2),L_{2,n},\tau_n)$ and coordinatewise output truncation to $[-K,K]$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: The finite component counts and component cube dimensions of the latent generator architectures are fixed as $n$ varies.
- $\epsilon_n$: $\epsilon_n$ denotes a positive deterministic approximation-tolerance sequence indexed by $n\in\mathbb N$, with its approximation role specified locally. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: $\epsilon_n>0$ for $n\in\mathbb N$, $\epsilon_n\to0$, and it bounds the distance from each point of $\tilde\Theta_\infty$ to an available point of $\Theta_n$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: In the radius definition, $\alpha_n=\epsilon_n+s_n$, where $\epsilon_n>0$ is chosen with sufficiently large constants in $\epsilon_n=O\left(W_{0,n}^{-1/d_{\max}^{\text{in}}}+\sum_{i=1}^2L_{i,n}^{-2/d_{\max}^U}+\tau_n(1-\log\tau_n)\right)$. In \cite[Theorem 2]{fournier2015rate}, used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the empirical generator concentration argument, $\epsilon_n$ is a local deterministic deviation tolerance in the bound $\sup_{\theta_{i,j}}W(P(f_{\theta_{i,j}}(Z_{i,j})),P_{m_n}(f_{\theta_{i,j}}(Z_{i,j})))\leqslant\epsilon_n+\epsilon'_n$; it is chosen as $\epsilon_n=Cm_n^{-1/(d_{\max}^U+2)}\log m_n$ with fixed $C>0$ sufficiently large. This local choice is distinct from the architecture approximation tolerance in the constraint radius.
- $s_n$: $s_n$ is a deterministic tolerance sequence indexed by $n$, specified by its displayed asymptotic order rather than by a unique numerical formula. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: $s_n>0$ is chosen as a sufficiently large constant multiple of the quantity in the displayed order $O\left(m_n^{-1/(D+2)}\log m_n+\frac{(L_{1,n}+L_{2,n})\log m_n}{\sqrt{m_n}}+n^{-1/\max\{2,D_U\}}\log^2 n+\log(nm_n)\lambda_n\right)$, where $D_U=\sum_{j=1}^{n_U}d_j^U$ includes the non-Gumbel latent variables only and $D=\max\{1,D_U\}$. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $s_n>0$ is chosen as a sufficiently large constant multiple of the quantity in the displayed order $O\left(m_n^{-1/(D+2)}\log m_n+\frac{(L_{1,n}+L_{2,n})\log m_n}{\sqrt{m_n}}+n^{-1/\max\{2,D_U\}}\log^2 n+\log(nm_n)\lambda_n\right)$, where $D_U=\sum_{j=1}^{n_U}d_j^U$ includes the non-Gumbel latent variables only and $D=\max\{1,D_U\}$.
- $\alpha_n$: $\alpha_n=\epsilon_n+s_n$ is a deterministic constraint tolerance sequence indexed by the observational sample size $n$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: $\alpha_n=\epsilon_n+s_n>0$, where the positive tolerances $\epsilon_n$ and $s_n$ are chosen with sufficiently large constants in their displayed asymptotic orders. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $\alpha_n=\epsilon_n+s_n>0$, where the positive tolerances $\epsilon_n$ and $s_n$ are chosen as sufficiently large constant multiples of the respective quantities in their displayed asymptotic orders.
- $\tau_n$: $\tau_n$ is a sequence indexed by $n$, used locally either as a generator temperature or as an additive tolerance in an approximate Lipschitz bound. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: $\tau_n$ is the additive tolerance in equation~\ref{eq:aprox_lip}, and $\tau_n\rightarrow0$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: In the network architecture and growth conditions, $\tau_n>0$ is the Gumbel-softmax generator temperature and $\tau_n\rightarrow0$; in the proof's application of the optimization proposition, its additive tolerance is assigned the separate value $4(1+\log(nm_n))\lambda_n$. In \cite[Theorem 2]{fournier2015rate}, used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: When verifying equation~\ref{eq:aprox_lip}, $\tau_n$ denotes the additive tolerance $4(1+\log(nm_n))\lambda_n$, which tends to zero under the stated regularization condition; this assignment does not identify it with the generator temperature.
- $\lambda_n$: $\lambda_n>0$, indexed by the observational sample size $n$, is the regularization parameter in $S_{\lambda_n}(P_{m_n}^{\hat{\mathcal{M}}}(\boldsymbol{V}),P_n^{\mathcal{M}^*}(\boldsymbol{V}))$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $\log(nm_n)\lambda_n\rightarrow0$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$.
- $d$: $d$ is local notation for a fixed dimension, a fixed metric, or a regression-difference function, with its role determined by its defining expression. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}: $d$ is the cube dimension in the homeomorphism $f:[0,1]^d\rightarrow K$ from Assumption~\ref{assumption:lower_bound}, rather than the ambient dimension $D$; the proof treats $d=0$ separately and uses the exponent $1/d$ only for $d\geqslant1$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:hilbert}: $d$ is the dimension of the cube $[0,1]^d$ being partitioned. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: $d$ is the ambient dimension of the target law on $\mathbb{R}^d$, distinct from the component cube dimensions $d_i^C$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: $d:M\times M\rightarrow[0,\infty)$ is the metric of the given space $(M,d)$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the proof's parameter space, $d(\theta,\theta')=\sum_{k=1}^{n_V}\|f_k-f_k'\|_\infty+\sum_{k=1}^{n_U}W(P(U_k),P(U_k'))$; occurrences of $d$ in imported distribution bounds retain their local dimension meaning. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $d$ is the common output dimension of the functions in $\mathcal F$ and the dimension used in the output test-function covering bound; the input law $\mu$ is on $\mathbb R^{d'}$. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: $d$ is the ambient dimension of the target law on $\mathbb R^d$, distinct from the component cube dimensions $d_i^C$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}: In the proof's test-function calculation, $s=(a,t)$ and $d(s)=\hat f_y(s)-f_y(s)$ on the allowed covariate domain $Q$; $f_y$ and $\hat f_y$ are the structural regression versions for the respective models.
- $d_1$: $d_1$ denotes a locally specified input or source dimension, including the input dimension in $\mathcal{NN}_{d_1,d_2}$, or an explicitly specified averaged metric on evaluation vectors. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:push-forward_err}: $K\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_1}$ is the common domain supporting $\mu$ and $\hat{\mu}$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the proof's notation for the combined maps $\hat{g}_i$, $d_1=1$. In \cite[Theorem 18.4]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $d_1$ is the averaged metric on length-$m$ evaluation vectors, $d_1(u,w)=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m|u_i-w_i|$, with $m$ a positive integer. In \cite[Theorem 17.1]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $d_1$ is the averaged metric on length-$N$ evaluation vectors, $d_1(u,w)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N|u_i-w_i|$; in the covering number appearing in the probability bound, $N=2m$.
- $d_2$: $d_2$ denotes the locally specified output or target dimension of a map, including the output dimension in $\mathcal{NN}_{d_1,d_2}$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:push-forward_err}: $F,\hat{F}:K\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{d_2}$, so $d_2$ is their common target dimension. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the proof's notation for the combined maps $\hat{g}_i$, $d_2=d$.
- $D$: $D$ is a deterministic geometric parameter specified by its local definition. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}, Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}, Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}, Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample_foral}, Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample}, Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the compact-support assumption, $D$ is the ambient Euclidean dimension in $K\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}$, rather than the cube dimension $d$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: In the constants controlling the treatment-effect comparison, $D=\max\left(\{1\}\cup\left\{\frac{n_i-1}{2}:V_i\text{ is categorical}\right\}\right)$ and $L_y=(LD+1)^{n_V}$; this $D$ can be nonintegral and equals $1$ when there are no categorical nodes. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: In the sampling tolerance $s_n$, $D=\max\{1,D_U\}$, where $D_U=\sum_{j=1}^{n_U}d_j^U$ includes the non-Gumbel latent variables only; this local $D$ is distinct from the ambient dimension in the compact-support assumption and from the categorical factor in the treatment-effect comparison. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}: In the proof's error recurrence, $D=\max\left(\{0\}\cup\{n_i-1:V_i\text{ is categorical}\}\right)$ and $A=\max\{1+L,1+LD/2\}$; this local $D$ is zero when there are no categorical nodes.
- $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}$: $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}=\max_{i\in[n_V]}d_i^{\text{in}}$, where $d_i^{\text{in}}$ is the input dimension of $f_i(\text{Pa}(V_i),\boldsymbol{U}_{V_i})$ in the canonical structural equations. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}\geqslant1$; when $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}=1$, the structural-network depth expression $\Theta(\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}})$ means $\Theta(1+\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}})$. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}>0$.
- $d_{\max}^{\text{out}}$: $d_{\max}^{\text{out}}=\max_{i\in[n_V]}d_i^{\text{out}}$, where $d_i^{\text{out}}=d_i$ for a continuous structural function and $d_i^{\text{out}}=n_i$ for a categorical propensity vector.
- $d_{\max}^U$: $d_{\max}^U=\max_{j\in[n_U]}d_j^U$, where $d_j^U$ is the dimension of a canonical latent variable $U_j$ whose distribution is approximated by a generator, distinct from the separately supplied categorical Gumbel noises. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $d_{\max}^U\geqslant1$; it remains the maximum individual non-Gumbel latent dimension, distinct from the total dimension $D_U=\sum_{j=1}^{n_U}d_j^U$ and $D=\max\{1,D_U\}$. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: $d_{\max}^U>0$.
- $d_{\mathcal{F}}$: $d_{\mathcal F}<\infty$ is a strict upper bound on the pseudo-dimensions of the scalar function classes specified in its local use. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: For every $j\in[d]$, $\mathcal F_j=\{x\mapsto f_j(x):f\in\mathcal F\}$ satisfies $\operatorname{Pdim}(\mathcal F_j)<d_{\mathcal F}$; the bound applies separately to each coordinate class.
- $C_{\mathcal{G}}(L,K)$: $C_{\mathcal G}(L,K;\{d_i,n_i\})$ denotes a numerical comparison coefficient whose permitted dependence is only on $L,K,\mathcal G$, the continuous output dimensions $d_i$, and the categorical cardinalities $n_i$.
- $C_W$: $C_W$ is a numerical comparison coefficient whose defining formula depends on the context. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:Lip_condition}: $C_W=4LK+2K\max\{L,1\}$, where $L$ bounds the Lipschitz constants of $f$ and $\hat{f}$ and $K$ bounds their absolute values. In Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}: $C_W=4L_yB+2B\max\{L_y,1\}$, where $L_y=(LD+1)^{n_V}$, $D=\max\left(\{1\}\cup\left\{\frac{n_i-1}{2}:V_i\text{ is categorical}\right\}\right)$, $q=\sum_{i:V_i\text{ is continuous}}d_i+\left|\{i:V_i\text{ is categorical}\}\right|$, and $B=K(1+2qL_y)$.
- $W_{0,n}$: $W_{0,n}$ is the width parameter of the structural-function approximation class $\mathcal{F}_{0,n}$, indexed by sample size $n$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $W_{0,n}\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$, as required by $\lim_{n\to\infty}\min\{\tau_n^{-1},W_{0,n},(\log(nm_n)\lambda_n)^{-1}\}=\infty$.
- $L_{i,n}$: $L_{i,n}$, $i=1,2$, indexes the depth sequences of the first and second parts of the latent-distribution generator architecture, with $n$ the sample-size index. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $L_{i,n}=\Theta(m_n^{d^U_{\max}/(2d^U_{\max}+4)})$ for $i=1,2$, with $m_n=\Omega(n)$.
- $p_i$: $p_i$ denotes a nonnegative scalar weight indexed by the coordinates, mixture terms, or partition cells of the local construction. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: $p_i=\mathbb{P}(C_i)$ for $i\in[N_C]$, and $\sum_{i=1}^{N_C}p_i=1$; these are the probabilities used to combine the support components. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:combin_err}: $p_1,\ldots,p_n\in[0,1]$ are arbitrary mixture weights satisfying $\sum_{k=1}^n p_k=1$, with no requirement that they be masses of connected support components. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:gumbel_err}: $p_1,\ldots,p_n>0$ are arbitrary positive softmax weights; normalization is not required in the statement. The proof normalizes them without loss of generality, and the limiting categorical probabilities are $p_i/\sum_{k=1}^n p_k$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sinkhorn_approx}: In the probability-simplex notation, $p_i$ is a coordinate satisfying $p_i\geqslant0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}: In the categorical case of the proof, $(p_1,\ldots,p_{n_i})=f(\text{pa}(v_k),\boldsymbol{u}_{V_k})$ is the conditional categorical probability vector evaluated at the displayed parent and latent values; its coordinates are nonnegative and sum to one. In Proposition~\ref{prop:equivalent_g_constrianed}: In the probability-simplex notation, $p_i$ is a coordinate satisfying $p_i\geqslant0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1$. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: $p_i=\mathbb P(C_i)$ for $i\in[N_C]$, and $\sum_{i=1}^{N_C}p_i=1$; these are the probabilities used to combine the support components. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}: In the printed partition construction at level $n+1$, $p_i=\mathbb P(C_{O_{n+1}(i)})$ for $1\leqslant i\leqslant2^{(n+1)d}$. Here $\mathbb P$ is the reduced cube measure and $C_{O_{n+1}(i)}$ is an ordered partition cube. These masses give the lengths of the corresponding parameter intervals and the denominators in the polygonal curve; domination by Lebesgue measure makes them positive. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the latent approximation construction, $p_i$ denotes the probability mass of component $C_i$ under the particular latent target law being approximated. These component probabilities sum to one and weight the component approximation errors and the hard selected mixture. In the categorical measurability argument, $p_i$ instead denotes coordinate $i$ of the categorical propensity vector evaluated at the structural input; these coordinates are nonnegative and sum to one, and zero coordinates are allowed.
- $p_\nu$: Writing $X=\text{Pa}(T)$, $p_\nu(t\mid X=x)$ is the conditional treatment density of $\nu(dt\mid x)$ with respect to the comparison measure $P(dt)$, so that $\nu(dt\mid x)=p_\nu(t\mid x)P(dt)$; its overlap lower bound holds for $\nu_X$-almost every $x$ and $t\in[t_1,t_2]$.
- $\delta$: $\delta>0$ denotes a locally specified positive real parameter. In Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $\delta$ in the overlap premise is the lower bound satisfying $p_\nu(t\mid\text{Pa}(T)=x)\geqslant\delta$ for $x$ almost surely and $t\in[t_1,t_2]$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:gumbel_err}: $\delta$ is the auxiliary threshold for the gaps between $G_i+\log p_i$; at the end of the proof it is chosen as $\delta=-\tau\log\tau$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample_foral}: In the proof, $\delta$ parameterizes $\mathcal{M}_\delta$: the covariate has an atom at $\delta$, and the outcome equation contains $X/\delta$ for $X\geqslant0$; the construction takes $\delta\rightarrow0$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $\delta$ is an arbitrary positive tolerance; the probability bound is for each fixed pair $\delta,\epsilon>0$. In the proof, $\mathcal H_\delta$ has uniform-norm covering radius $\delta/2$, so replacing a test function by its representative contributes at most $\delta$ to the difference of its empirical and population integrals. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the simulation-concentration argument, the empirical Wasserstein bound is applied with $\delta=r_n$, where $H_n=1+L_{1,n}+L_{2,n}$ and $r_n=m_n^{-1/(D+2)}\log m_n+H_nm_n^{-1/2}\log m_n$; its other tolerance is $\epsilon=A_0r_n$. In \cite[Theorem VIII.1]{perekrestenkoHighDimensionalDistributionGeneration2022a}, used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: For a component of positive dimension $q=d_i^C$, $\delta=1/\lceil\sqrt q(q+1)n(n-1)\rceil$ is the source quantization parameter, and the quantization mesh is $\delta/n$; here $n=\lfloor(W_1/A_q)^{1/q}\rfloor$ for $W_1\geqslant A_q2^q$, with $A_q\geqslant1$ depending only on $q$. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: Separately from the overlap parameter, the proof's simulation-concentration argument chooses the local tolerance $\delta=r_n$, where $H_n=1+L_{1,n}+L_{2,n}$ and $r_n=m_n^{-1/(D+2)}\log m_n+H_nm_n^{-1/2}\log m_n$, for sufficiently large $n$; the other tolerance is $\epsilon=Cr_n$ for a sufficiently large fixed positive constant $C$.
- $c$: $c$ denotes a locally specified scalar, categorical configuration, or real-valued function, according to its defining expression. In Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample}, Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample_foral}: $c>0$ is chosen together with $\mathcal{M}^*$ before quantifying over $\epsilon>0$, and is independent of $\epsilon$; it is a strict lower bound for $|\text{ATE}_{\mathcal{M}^*}-\text{ATE}_{\mathcal{M}_\epsilon}|$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sinkhorn_approx}: In the proof's final self-term calculation, $c=W_{1,\lambda}(\nu,\nu)$ is the entropy-regularized self-transport value, with $|c|\leqslant(1+2\log m)\lambda$; it is nonpositive under the specified entropy convention. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $c>0$ is the concentration constant multiplying $n\epsilon^2$ in the negative term of the probability exponent; it depends only on $d,K$ and is independent of $n,\delta,\epsilon$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}: In the proof, $c(t)=\int\hat f_y(a,t)\nu_A(da)-\int\hat f_y(a,t)\mu_A(da)$ is the contribution from changing the observational marginal of $A$, with $\nu_A$ and $\mu_A$ the respective observational marginals. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the observational concentration argument, $c$ ranges over the fixed finite set of possible complete categorical label vectors: $p_c=P(C=c)$ and $\mu_c=P((U_1,\ldots,U_{n_U})\mid C=c)$, the latter being used for $p_c>0$. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: In categorical types $(u,c)$ and conditioning expressions, $c$ is a complete categorical label vector, with $p_c=P(C=c)$ and $\mu_c=P((U_1,\ldots,U_{n_U})\mid C=c)$ for $p_c>0$. Separately, in the concentration exponent $-cC^2m_nr_n^2$, $c>0$ is a fixed concentration constant.
- $t_1$: $t_1$ is a real scalar whose role is local to the intervention interval or the Lipschitz comparison. In Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $t_1$ is the fixed lower endpoint of the intervention interval $[t_1,t_2]$. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $t_1<t_2$, and $\mu_T$ is the uniform probability law on $[t_1,t_2]$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:Lip_condition}: In the proof, $t_1$ is the treatment coordinate of the first arbitrary comparison point $(t_1,y_1)$ in $\{(t,y):\|(t,y)\|_\infty\leqslant K\}$.
- $t_2$: $t_2$ is a real scalar whose role is local to the intervention interval or the Lipschitz comparison. In Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $t_2$ is the fixed upper endpoint of the intervention interval $[t_1,t_2]$. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $t_1<t_2$, and $\mu_T$ is the uniform probability law on $[t_1,t_2]$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:Lip_condition}: In the proof, $t_2$ is the treatment coordinate of the second arbitrary comparison point $(t_2,y_2)$ in $\{(t,y):\|(t,y)\|_\infty\leqslant K\}$.
- $\Delta_n$: $\Delta_n$ denotes a subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose coordinates sum to one. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sinkhorn_approx}: $\Delta_n=\{(p_1,\ldots,p_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1,\ p_i\geqslant0\}$ is the probability simplex. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:gumbel_err}: In the proof, $\Delta_n=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n:\sum_{k=1}^n x_k=1\}$ is the domain of the transportation map; the vectors $X^\tau$ and $X^0$ themselves have nonnegative coordinates. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}, Proposition~\ref{prop:equivalent_g_constrianed}: $\Delta_n=\{(p_1,\ldots,p_n)\in\mathbb R^n:\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1,\ p_i\geqslant0\}$ is the probability simplex.
- $M$: $M$ is the ambient space equipped with the metric $d$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the proof, $M=\mathcal F_{V_1}\times\cdots\times\mathcal F_{V_{n_V}}\times\prod_{j=1}^{n_U}\mathcal P([-K,K]^{d_j^U})$. For continuous $V_i$, $\mathcal F_{V_i}=\mathcal F_{\hat L_f}^K([-K,K]^{d_{i,\text{in}}^V},[-K,K]^{d_{i,\text{out}}^V})$, with uniform output $1$-norm bound $K$ and Lipschitz bound $\hat L_f$. For categorical $V_i$, $\mathcal F_{V_i}=\{p:[-K,K]^{d_{i,\text{in}}^V}\rightarrow\Delta_{n_i}:\operatorname{Lip}(p)\leqslant\hat L_f\}$. Here $\mathcal P(A)$ is the set of probability measures on $A$, and $d(\theta,\theta')=\sum_{k=1}^{n_V}\|f_k-f_k'\|_\infty+\sum_{k=1}^{n_U}W(P(U_k),P(U_k'))$.
- $\Theta_n$: $\Theta_n\subset M$ is the parameter set indexed by $n\in\mathbb{N}$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: $\Theta_1\subset\Theta_2\subset\cdots\subset\Theta_n\subset\cdots$, and every $\theta_0\in\tilde\Theta_\infty$ has a point $\theta\in\Theta_n$ with $d(\theta,\theta_0)\leqslant\epsilon_n$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: $\Theta_n=\hat{\mathcal F}_{V_1,n}\times\cdots\times\hat{\mathcal F}_{V_{n_V},n}\times\mathcal P_n$. For continuous $V_i$, $\hat{\mathcal F}_{V_i,n}=\{\hat f_i\in\mathcal F_{0,n}:\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K\}$, with the supremum over the full structural input domain. For categorical $V_i$, $\hat{\mathcal F}_{V_i,n}$ consists of $x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1$ with $q\in\mathcal F_{0,n}$ satisfying $q(x)\in[0,\infty)^{n_i}$, $\|q(x)\|_1>0$ for every structural input $x$, and $\operatorname{Lip}(x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1)\leqslant\hat L_f$. Here $\mathcal P_n=\{P(\boldsymbol U):\boldsymbol U\text{ is the latent distribution of }\hat{\mathcal M}\in\text{NCM}_{\mathcal G}(\mathcal F_{0,n},\mathcal F_{1,n})\}$, identified with its tuple of independent latent marginal laws. This product records population model parameters; the empirical optimization ranges over their network representations, including distinct representations inducing identical latent population laws.
- $\Theta_\infty$: $\Theta_\infty=\overline{\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}\Theta_n}$, with closure taken in the ambient metric space $(M,d)$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: $\Theta_\infty$ is compact and contains the nested sets $\Theta_n$; $\{\theta\in\Theta_\infty:g(\theta)=0\}$ is nonempty. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: The closure is that of the neural-model parameter sets in the metric $d(\theta,\theta')=\sum_{k=1}^{n_V}\|f_k-f_k'\|_\infty+\sum_{k=1}^{n_U}W(P(U_k),P(U_k'))$ on the product space of structural functions and latent probability measures.
- $\tilde{\Theta}_\infty$: $\tilde\Theta_\infty$ is a compact subset of $\Theta_\infty$ approximated by $\Theta_n$: for every $\theta_0\in\tilde\Theta_\infty$ and every $n$, some $\theta\in\Theta_n$ satisfies $d(\theta,\theta_0)\leqslant\epsilon_n$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: $\{\theta\in\tilde\Theta_\infty:g(\theta)=0\}$ is nonempty.
- $\delta_n$: $\delta_n$ denotes a deterministic error tolerance indexed by $n$ and tending to zero. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: $\delta_n>0$ for $n\in\mathbb N$, and $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_\infty}|g_n(\theta)-g(\theta)|\leqslant\delta_n$. In \cite[Theorem 2]{fournier2015rate}, used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: For sufficiently large $n$, the local observational latent deviation tolerance is $\delta_n=C_1n^{-1/\max\{d_{\max}^U,2\}}\log^2 n$, with fixed $C_1>0$ chosen sufficiently large; this is distinct from the abstract uniform constraint-error tolerance.
- $g_n$: $\{g_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of real-valued constraint functions on $\Theta_\infty$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: Each $g_n$ is continuous and nonnegative, with $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_\infty}|g_n(\theta)-g(\theta)|\leqslant\delta_n$, and the approximate Lipschitz bound has common coefficient $L_g$ and additive tolerance $\tau_n$. In \cite[Theorem 2]{fournier2015rate}, used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: The notation is the empirical constraint $g_n(\theta)=S_{\lambda_n}(P_n^{\theta^*}(\boldsymbol V),P_{m_n}^{\theta}(\boldsymbol V))$, compared with the population constraint $g(\theta)=W(P^{\theta^*}(\boldsymbol V),P^{\theta}(\boldsymbol V))$.
- $g$: $g$ denotes a real-valued function on the domain specified by its local use. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}: In the proof, $g$ ranges over real-valued $1$-Lipschitz Wasserstein dual test functions of $(\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{t},v_1,\ldots,v_k)$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:push-forward_err}: In the proof, $g:\mathbb{R}^{d_2}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is an arbitrary $1$-Lipschitz test function. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:Lip_condition}: In the proof, $g$ ranges over real-valued $1$-Lipschitz test functions of $(t,y)$ in the Wasserstein dual formula. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: $g:\Theta_\infty\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is the limiting constraint, with $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_\infty}|g_n(\theta)-g(\theta)|\leqslant\delta_n$; its zero set defines the limiting feasible regions. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: $g(\theta)=W(P^{\theta^*}(\boldsymbol{V}),P^\theta(\boldsymbol{V}))$ is the population observational discrepancy, rather than an empirical discrepancy. In \cite[Theorem 18.4]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $g$ ranges over functions in a nonempty class $\mathcal G\subset\{g:X\rightarrow[0,1]\}$ with finite pseudo-dimension $v$. No Lipschitz condition on $g$ is specified. In \cite[Theorem 17.1]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $g:T\times X\rightarrow[0,1]$ is jointly Borel, where $T$ and $X$ are standard Borel spaces, and $\mathcal G=\{g(t,\cdot):t\in T\}\ne\varnothing$. For each $t\in T$, the squared loss is $(g(t,x)-y)^2$. No pseudo-dimension bound or Lipschitz condition on $g$ is imposed.
- $L_g$: $L_g$ is a finite nonnegative Lipschitz bound. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: $L_g$ is independent of $n$ and is the coefficient in $|g_n(\theta_1)-g_n(\theta_2)|\leqslant L_g d(\theta_1,\theta_2)+\tau_n$; the limiting function $g$ is $L_g$-Lipschitz. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:Lip_condition}: In the proof, $L_g=2K\max\{L,1\}$ bounds the Lipschitz constant of $g_0(t,y)=(\hat f(t)-f(t))y$ on $\{(t,y):\|(t,y)\|_\infty\leqslant K\}$.
- $B$: $B$ is a locally specified measurable test set or positive scalar bound. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the componentwise lower-bound premise, $B$ ranges over measurable subsets of $[0,1]^{d_i^C}$; the component measure and its parameterizing map satisfy the domination inequality of Assumption~\ref{assumption:lower_bound} on these sets. Separately, in the proof's clipping and mixing estimates, $B>0$ is a fixed scalar chosen so that every support component lies in $[-B,B]^d$, and the second-block outputs are clipped into this box. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}, Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}, Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample_foral}, Proposition~\ref{prop:counterexample}, Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: In the lower-bound premise, $B$ ranges over measurable subsets of $[0,1]^d$ and $\mathbb{P}(f(B))\geqslant C_f\lambda(B)$; for a component with dimension $d_i^C$, the corresponding test sets lie in $[0,1]^{d_i^C}$. In Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}: $B$ is the scalar bound $B=K(1+2qL_y)$, where $q=\sum_{i:V_i\text{ is continuous}}d_i+|\{i:V_i\text{ is categorical}\}|$ and $L_y=(LD+1)^{n_V}$; it enters $C_W=4L_yB+2B\max\{L_y,1\}$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}, Lemma~\ref{lemma:push-forward_err}, Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}, Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}, \cite[Theorem 18.4]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: In a push-forward expression $f_\#\mu(B)$, $B$ is an arbitrary measurable subset of the codomain of $f$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}: In the proof's error recurrence, $B=\max\left(\{1\}\cup\{d_i:V_i\text{ is continuous}\}\cup\{n_i(n_i-1)/2:V_i\text{ is categorical}\}\right)$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the proof's model-comparison recurrence, $B$ is a fixed positive bound on the coefficients of the structural approximation errors, chosen together with $A\geqslant1$ so that $e_{k+1}\leqslant Ae_k+B d(\theta,\theta')$. Separately, in the derivation of the pseudo-dimension bound, $B=CH_n^2$, where $H_n=1+L_{1,n}+L_{2,n}$ and $C$ is the constant in that derivation; this latter scalar may vary with $n$. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: In the structural extension and approximation construction, $B=B_0H^{n_V}$, where $m=d_{\max}^{\text{in}}$, $H=1+2Lm$, and $B_0=\max\left(\{1,R,K\}\cup\{n_i:V_i\text{ is categorical}\}\cup\{\|f_i(a_i)\|_\infty:V_i\text{ is continuous}\}\right)$; $a_i$ has zero in each real input coordinate and one in each categorical input coordinate. This fixed positive scalar is independent of the intervention and network budgets and defines the structural input cubes $Q_i=[-B,B]^{m_i}$. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: In the proof's model-comparison recurrence, $B$ is a fixed positive bound on the coefficients of the structural approximation errors, chosen together with $A\geqslant1$ so that $e_{k+1}\leqslant Ae_k+B d(\theta,\theta')$; it is independent of the sample size and the compared model parameters.
- $\mathcal{N}_1$: $\mathcal{N}_1(\epsilon,\mathcal{F},n)=\sup_{x_1,\ldots,x_n}\mathcal{N}(\epsilon,\{(f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_n)):f\in\mathcal{F}\},\|\cdot\|_1)$, where the points range over the domain of $\mathcal{F}$ and the norm is the printed $\ell_1$ norm without a factor $1/n$. In \cite[Theorem 18.4]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $\mathcal N_1^{\mathrm{avg}}(\epsilon,\mathcal G,m)$ is the supremum over $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in X$ of the covering numbers of $\{(g(x_1),\ldots,g(x_m)):g\in\mathcal G\}$ in $d_1(u,w)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m|u_i-w_i|$, for $\epsilon>0$ and positive integers $m$. This averaged covering number is distinct from the covering number defined with the unnormalized $\ell_1$ norm. In \cite[Theorem 17.1]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $\mathcal N_1^{\mathrm{avg}}(r,\mathcal G,N)$ is the supremum over $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in X$ of the covering number of $\{(g(x_1),\ldots,g(x_N)):g\in\mathcal G\}$ in $d_1(u,w)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N|u_i-w_i|$. The probability bound uses $r=\epsilon/16$ and $N=2m$. This averaged covering number is distinct from the covering number defined with the unnormalized $\ell_1$ norm.
- $\mathcal{H}_\delta$: $\mathcal H_\delta\subseteq\mathcal H$ is a finite $\delta/2$-net in the uniform norm of $\mathcal H=\{h:[-K,K]^d\rightarrow\mathbb R:h(0)=0,\ |h(x)-h(y)|\leqslant\|x-y\|\}$, for $\delta>0$.
- $h$: $h$ denotes the auxiliary function or positive grid spacing defined in its surrounding passage. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: $h(w,X)=w^{\mathsf{T}}X\in\mathbb{R}^d$, where $w$ has $N_C$ coordinates, $X$ collects the $N_C$ component outputs, and the stated region is $\|w\|_1=1$, $\|X\|_\infty\leqslant K$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:Lip_condition}: $h(t)=(\hat{f}(t)-f(t))\hat{f}(t)$ is the real-valued auxiliary function in the proof, with the stated Lipschitz constant $L_h=4LK$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sinkhorn_approx}: $h(T)=1-\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^m T_{ij}\log T_{ij}$ is the entropy expression for $T\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)$, with $0\log0=0$. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $h$ is a scalar test function in $\mathcal H=\{h:[-K,K]^d\rightarrow\mathbb R:h(0)=0,\ |h(x)-h(y)|\leqslant\|x-y\|\}$, so its values lie in $[-dK,dK]$; the concentration argument first fixes such an $h$ and uses $z_f=\sqrt{(h\circ f+dK)/(2dK)}$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: In the structural interpolation construction, $h=2K/R>0$ is the side length of a grid cell obtained by dividing each coordinate of $[-K,K]^m$ into $R$ equal intervals; $I_hf$ is the resulting piecewise affine interpolant. In Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}: In the proof, $s=(a,t)$ and $h(s)=(\hat f_y(s)-f_y(s))\hat f_y(s)$ on the bounded covariate domain $Q$. The structural regression versions satisfy $|f_y|,|\hat f_y|\leqslant B$ there, and $|h(s)-h(s')|\leqslant4BL_y\|s-s'\|$.
- $m$: $m$ is a local integer parameter whose role is determined by the objects in the surrounding passage. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}: In $\gamma_m(t)\in C_{k,n-1}$ for all $m\geqslant n$, $m$ is a later curve level. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the Sinkhorn comparison, the second probability-vector length is the simulation count $m_n$, giving the factor $\log(nm_n)$. In the structural interpolation argument, $m$ is the input dimension of $f:[-K,K]^m\rightarrow\mathbb R^{m'}$; the construction treats $m\geqslant1$ by triangulation and $m=0$ by exact constant representation. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sinkhorn_approx}: $m\geqslant1$ is the length of $\nu\in\Delta_m$, indexing the points $y_1,\ldots,y_m$, and the number of columns of its transportation plan with $\mu\in\Delta_n$; it need not count only positive coordinates or distinct points. In \cite[Theorem 18.4]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $m\geqslant1$ is an arbitrary integer counting evaluation points in the averaged empirical covering and packing numbers. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: In the structural interpolation argument, $m$ is the input dimension of $f:[-K,K]^m\rightarrow\mathbb R^{m'}$; the construction treats $m\geqslant1$ by triangulation and $m=0$ by exact constant representation. In \cite[Theorem 17.1]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $m\geqslant1$ is the number of independent observations $(x_i,y_i)$ with law $P$ in the empirical squared loss; $\mathcal N_1^{\mathrm{avg}}(\epsilon/16,\mathcal G,2m)$ uses $2m$ evaluation points. In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}: In the recurrence argument, $m=n_V-n_T$ is the number of nonintervened observed nodes. The argument includes $m=0$, with an empty geometric sum. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: In the structural extension and approximation construction, $m=d_{\max}^{\text{in}}>0$ is the largest structural input dimension, while $m_i=d_i^{\text{in}}$ is the input dimension at node $i$.
- $\|\cdot\|_\infty$: $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ denotes the infinity norm on vectors and its uniform extension to functions: $\|f\|_\infty=\sup_{x\in\operatorname{dom}(f)}\|f(x)\|_\infty$.
- $R$: $R$ is a locally specified shape-ratio functional or fixed positive intervention bound. In Proposition~\ref{prop:holder_curve}: $R(\mathcal C)=\max_{i,k}|a_i^k-b_i^k|/\min_{i,k}|a_i^k-b_i^k|$ for the finite collection $\mathcal C=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}$ with $C_k=\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i^k,b_i^k]$, wherever the denominator is positive. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: $R>0$ is fixed before choosing $\hat{\mathcal M}$ and bounds each continuous intervention value by $\|t_i\|_\infty\leqslant R$; the implicit approximation constant may depend on $R$, which remains fixed as the network budgets tend to infinity and $\tau\downarrow0$.
- $S$: $S$ denotes the auxiliary object defined locally in its surrounding argument.
