In Theorem~\ref{thm:approximation}: In the proof, $S=\sum_{i=1}^{n_V}\|f_i-\hat{f}_i\|_\infty$ is the summed structural-function approximation error. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: In the categorical normalization argument, at the structural input $x=(\text{pa}(v_k),\boldsymbol{u}_{V_k})$, $S=\|\hat f_i(x)-f_i(x)\|_\infty$, where $f_i(x)$ is the normalized true propensity vector and $\hat f_i(x)$ is the unnormalized nonnegative approximant. The comparison is with $\hat f_i(x)/\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1$ wherever its denominator is nonzero. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}, \cite[Theorem 18.4]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $S$ in $\mathcal{N}(\epsilon,S,\|\cdotp\|_1)$ is the set to be covered; the unnormalized empirical construction uses $\{(f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_N)):f\in\mathcal F\}$ for specified input points. For $\mathcal{N}_1^{\mathrm{avg}}(\epsilon,\mathcal G,m)$, the evaluation set is instead $\{(g(x_1),\ldots,g(x_m)):g\in\mathcal G\}$, equipped with $d_1(u,w)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m|u_i-w_i|$. In \cite[Theorem 17.1]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: The set covered in $\mathcal{N}_1^{\mathrm{avg}}(r,\mathcal G,N)$ is $S=\{(g(x_1),\ldots,g(x_N)):g\in\mathcal G\}$ for specified evaluation points, equipped with $d_1(u,w)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N|u_i-w_i|$; the bound uses $N=2m$.
- $\mathcal{N}$: $\mathcal{N}$ denotes either the covering-number functional when supplied with covering arguments, or a locally quantified causal model. In Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}, \cite[Theorem 18.4]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $\mathcal{N}(\epsilon,S,\|\cdotp\|_1)$ denotes the covering number of the evaluation set $S$ in the summed $1$-norm; the separately marked averaged covering numbers use the averaged empirical metric. In Proposition~\ref{prop:Lip_ATE}: In the proof, $\mathcal{N}\in\{\mathcal{M},\hat{\mathcal{M}}\}$ ranges over the two causal models when bounding their structural regression functions. In \cite[Theorem 17.1]{anthony1999neural}, used in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein}: $\mathcal{N}_1^{\mathrm{avg}}(r,\mathcal G,N)$ is the supremum over $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in X$ of the covering number of $\{(g(x_1),\ldots,g(x_N)):g\in\mathcal G\}$ in $d_1(u,w)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N|u_i-w_i|$; the concentration bound uses $r=\epsilon/16$ and $N=2m$.
- $\theta_{\mathcal{M}}$: $\theta_{\mathcal{M}}=(f_1,\ldots,f_{n_V},P(U_1),\ldots,P(U_{n_U}))$ represents a canonical SCM through the functions in (\ref{eq:structure_equation}) and the population marginal laws of its non-Gumbel latent coordinates, called the uniform parts in the parameterization; the categorical standard Gumbel laws are not additional tuple coordinates.
- $\mathcal{M}^{\theta}$: $\mathcal{M}^\theta$ is the canonical SCM with structural functions and non-Gumbel latent marginal laws specified by $\theta$, using the given causal graph and canonical latent incidence structure; the standard Gumbel laws in categorical equations are supplied by the canonical construction.
- $\theta^*$: $\theta^*$ denotes a distinguished parameter point whose role is specified by the local optimization or causal-model parameterization. In Proposition~\ref{prop:convg_opt}: $\theta^*\in\Theta_\infty$ is a minimizer of (\ref{eq:opt*}), satisfying $g(\theta^*)=0$ and $f(\theta^*)=f^*$; it is distinct in notation and role from $\tilde\theta^*$, the minimizer over $\tilde\Theta_\infty$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: $\theta^*$ is the canonical parameter tuple of the underlying SCM, containing its structural functions and non-Gumbel latent marginal laws; $\tilde\Theta_\infty=\{\theta^*\}$. In Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: $\theta^*$ is the canonical parameter tuple representing the underlying SCM $\mathcal M^*$, containing its structural functions and non-Gumbel latent population marginal laws.
- $\theta'$: $\theta'=(f_1',\ldots,f_{n_V}',P(U_1'),\ldots,P(U_{n_U}'))\in M$ is a second canonical model parameter tuple, with $f_i'\in\mathcal{F}_{V_i}$ and non-Gumbel latent marginal laws $P(U_j')\in\mathcal{P}([-K,K]^{d_j^U})$, compared with $\theta$ through $d(\theta,\theta')$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}, Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}: When $\theta'$ indexes an empirical candidate law, its candidate index additionally specifies a network representation; the population tuple alone need not determine $P_{m_n}^{\theta'}$ on the common simulation inputs.
- $P^\theta$: $P^\theta$ denotes the population law induced by the canonical SCM $\mathcal{M}^\theta$ represented by the structural functions and latent marginal laws in $\theta$; its argument specifies the variables or intervention whose law is taken, and it is distinct from the empirical laws $P_n^\theta$ and $P_{m_n}^\theta$.
- $\mathcal{F}_{V_i}$: $\mathcal{F}_{V_i}$ is the population structural-function class for $i\in[n_V]$ on the indicated input cube, with the continuous or categorical branch selected by the type of $V_i$; in the categorical branch, $\|f(x)\|_1=1$ at each structural input $x$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: The bounded Lipschitz class used in the population optimization has $\sup_x\|f(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ and $\operatorname{Lip}(f)\leqslant L$ on the full structural input domain; categorical structural functions are nonnegative normalized propensity vectors.
- $d_{i,\text{in}}^{V}$: $d_{i,\text{in}}^{V}$, for $i\in[n_V]$, is the input coordinate dimension of the structural function $f_i$, whose arguments are $\text{Pa}(V_i)$ and $\boldsymbol{U}_{V_i}$; the population function-class construction uses the domain $[-K,K]^{d_{i,\text{in}}^{V}}$.
- $d_{i,\text{out}}^{V}$: $d_{i,\text{out}}^{V}$ is the output dimension of the canonical structural function $f_i$, for $i\in[n_V]$, equal to $d_i$ when $V_i$ is continuous and to $n_i$ when $V_i$ is categorical.
- $d_j^U$: $d_j^U$, for $j\in[n_U]$, is the Euclidean coordinate dimension of the indexed latent variable $U_j$, excluding the separately introduced categorical Gumbel noises.
- $\mathcal{P}$: $\mathcal{P}(K)$ is the space of Borel probability measures on the set $K$, equipped with Wasserstein-1 distance, which metrizes weak convergence on the compact domains used here.
- $\mathcal{P}_n$: $\mathcal{P}_n=\{P(\boldsymbol{U}):\boldsymbol{U}\text{ is the latent collection of }\hat{\mathcal{M}}\in\text{NCM}_{\mathcal{G}}(\mathcal{F}_{0,n},\mathcal{F}_{1,n})\}$ is the population latent-law class indexed by $n$, rather than a class of empirical latent measures. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: In the proof's population parameterization $\Theta_n$, $\mathcal{P}_n$ is identified with $\mathcal{P}_{n,1}\times\cdots\times\mathcal{P}_{n,n_U}$, the tuple of generated non-Gumbel marginal laws on $[-K,K]^{d_j^U}$, $j\in[n_U]$; the separately prescribed categorical Gumbel noises are not additional coordinates of this tuple. Each generated marginal law integrates the generator's uniform input and Gumbel-softmax randomness. This population-law tuple does not determine a candidate's common-draw empirical distribution: different network representations of the same latent laws can have different empirical distributions.
- $\hat{\mathcal{F}}_{V_i,n}$: $\hat{\mathcal{F}}_{V_i,n}$ is the node-specific structural function class at index $n$, for $i\in[n_V]$, with categorical normalization interpreted pointwise as $x\mapsto f(x)/\|f(x)\|_1$ wherever $\|f(x)\|_1>0$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: For categorical $V_i$, $\hat{\mathcal{F}}_{V_i,n}$ consists of the maps $x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1$ with $q\in\mathcal{F}_{0,n}$ satisfying $q(x)\in[0,\infty)^{n_i}$ and $\|q(x)\|_1>0$ for every structural input $x$, and $\operatorname{Lip}(x\mapsto q(x)/\|q(x)\|_1)\leqslant\hat L_f$. For continuous $V_i$, the candidate structural class is $\{\hat f_i\in\mathcal F_{0,n}:\sup_x\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K\}$, where the supremum is over the full structural input domain.
- $\hat{g}_1^i$: For $i\in[N_C]$, $\hat{g}_1^i$ denotes the chosen first generator block for component $C_i$, with scalar input and $d_i^C$ output coordinates. In the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: For $d_i^C>0$, $\hat{g}_1^i$ is the coordinatewise deep ReLU approximation of the curve $\gamma_i:[0,1]\rightarrow[0,1]^{d_i^C}$ satisfying $(\gamma_i)_{\#}\lambda=(g_2^i)^{-1}_{\#}\mu_i$; its coordinate networks have width $12$ and depth $L_1$, its combined width is $\Theta(d_i^C)$, and $\|\hat{g}_1^i-\gamma_i\|_\infty\leqslant O(L_1^{-2/d_i^C})$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: For $d_i^C=0$, $\hat{g}_1^i$ is the unique map to $[0,1]^0$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: For $d_i^C>0$, $\hat{g}_1^i$ is a quantized ReLU network of width $W_1$ and depth $\Theta(d_i^C)$, chosen so that $W((g_2^i)^{-1}_{\#}\mu_i,P(\hat{g}_1^i(U_i)))\leqslant O(W_1^{-1/d_i^C})$. In \cite[Theorem VIII.1]{perekrestenkoHighDimensionalDistributionGeneration2022a}, used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: For a component of positive dimension $q=d_i^C$, $\hat{g}_1^i$ is the quantized ReLU component generator of width $W_1$ and depth $\Theta(q)$ satisfying $W((g_2^i)^{-1}_{\#}\mu_i,P(\hat{g}_1^i(U_i)))\leqslant O(W_1^{-1/q})$. The source construction uses integer depth parameter $s=1$, quantization parameter $\delta=1/\lceil\sqrt q(q+1)n(n-1)\rceil$, and mesh $\delta/n$, where $n=\lfloor(W_1/A_q)^{1/q}\rfloor$ for $W_1\geqslant A_q2^q$ and $A_q\geqslant1$ depends only on $q$.
- $U_i$: $U_i$ denotes the index-$i$ random variable in the locally specified latent or generator-input family. In Corollary~\ref{corollary:deep_nn}: In the SCM notation, $U_i$ is a non-Gumbel latent variable of the model being approximated, with its own latent dimension and population law; scalar uniform variables appearing in the component-generator construction are inputs used to approximate that law. In Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}, the result split from Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the component-generator construction, $U_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1])$ for $i\in[N_C]$; $i$ indexes connected support components, and $U_i$ is the scalar input to $\hat g_1^i$. In \cite[Theorem VIII.1]{perekrestenkoHighDimensionalDistributionGeneration2022a}, used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:wide_nn}: In the component-generator construction, $U_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1])$ for $i\in[N_C]$; $i$ indexes connected support components, and $U_i$ is the scalar input to $\hat g_1^i$. In \cite[Theorem 2]{fournier2015rate}, used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:consistency}: $U_i$, $i\in[n_U]$, is a non-Gumbel latent variable with values in $[-K,K]^{d_i^U}$ under the locally specified model law $P^\theta$ or $P^{\theta^*}$; the scalar uniform generator inputs are $Z_{i,j}$. The vector $(U_1,\ldots,U_{n_U})$ has total dimension $D_U=\sum_{i=1}^{n_U}d_i^U$.
- $s$: $s$ denotes the fixed integer depth parameter $s=1$, distinct from the quantization parameter $\delta$ and the quantization mesh $\delta/n$.

**Objections raised during the review and withdrawn.** The paper's owner showed that each misreads the paper; the printed statement stands under the reading given.

- **a condition or definition of the paper.** A network in $\mathcal{NN}_{k_1,k_2}(W,L)$ has $L$ hidden layers, each of width at most $W$, followed by the affine output layer (width at most $W$ and exactly $W$ give the same class of functions: a narrower layer is padded with zero units). The covering number $\mathcal{N}(\epsilon,S,\|\cdot\|_1)$ is that of the cited source (Anthony and Bartlett): the least size of a subset $C\subseteq S$ such that every point of $S$ lies at $\ell_1$ distance strictly less than $\epsilon$ from some point of $C$.
- **a condition or definition of the paper.** A network in $\mathcal{NN}_{k_1,k_2}(W,L)$ has $L$ hidden layers, each of width at most $W$, followed by the affine output layer (width at most $W$ and exactly $W$ give the same class of functions: a narrower layer is padded with zero units). The covering number $\mathcal{N}(\epsilon,S,\|\cdot\|_1)$ is that of the cited source (Anthony and Bartlett): the least size of a subset $C\subseteq S$ such that every point of $S$ lies at $\ell_1$ distance strictly less than $\epsilon$ from some point of $C$.

  ```lean
  def AnthonyBartlettSquaredLoss : Sort 0 :=
    ∀ (X : Type) (_mX : MeasurableSpace X) [StandardBorelSpace X]
      (G : Set (X → ℝ)), G.Nonempty → BorelParametrizedClass G →
      ∀ hG : (∀ g ∈ G, Measurable g ∧ ∀ x, g x ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1),
      ∀ P : ProbabilityMeasure (X × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1),
        ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → ∀ eps : ℝ, 0 < eps → eps < 1 →
          (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin m => (P : Measure (X × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)))).completion
            {z : Fin m → X × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 | ∃ g ∈ G,
              |(∫ xy : X × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, (g xy.1 - xy.2.val)^2
                  ∂(P : Measure (X × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1))) -
                (m : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, (g (z i).1 - (z i).2.val)^2| ≥ eps} ≤
            4 * (N1avg (eps/16) G (2*m) (fun g hg => (hG g hg).2)).toENNReal *
              ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-(eps^2 * m)/32))
  ```

  The passage of the proof:

  > The cited assertion used in Lemma~\ref{lemma:sup_wasserstein} is the following restricted form of Theorem 17.1 in \cite{anthony1999neural}, with its standing measurability condition. Let $X$ and $T$ be standard Borel spaces, let $g:T\times X\rightarrow[0,1]$ be jointly Borel, and put $\mathcal G=\{g(t,\cdot):t\in T\}\ne\varnothing$. For every Borel probability distribution $P$ on $X\times[0,1]$, every $0<\epsilon<1$ and every positive integer $m$,
  > \[
  > P^m\left\{\text{some }t\in T\text{ has }\left|\mathbb E_{(x,y)\sim P}(g(t,x)-y)^2-\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m(g(t,x_i)-y_i)^2\right|\geqslant\epsilon\right\}
  > \leqslant4\mathcal N_1^{\mathrm{avg}}(\epsilon/16,\mathcal G,2m)\exp(-\epsilon^2m/32).
  > \]
  > Here the sample consists of independent draws from $P$, the probability is taken in its completion, and $\mathcal N_1^{\mathrm{avg}}(r,\mathcal G,N)$ is the supremum over $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in X$ of the covering number of the evaluation vectors in the metric $N^{-1}\sum_i|u_i-v_i|$.

  What Lean assumes for it: `Papers.TbsNeuralCausalPi.AnthonyBartlettPacking` (`Setup/CitedResults.lean:164`)

  ```lean
  def AnthonyBartlettPacking : Sort 0 :=
    ∀ (X : Type) (G : Set (X → ℝ)), G.Nonempty →
      ∀ hG : (∀ g ∈ G, ∀ x, g x ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1),
      ∀ v : ℕ,
        Causalean.Stat.Concentration.HasPseudoDimAtMost (fun g : G => g.val) v →
        ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → ∀ eps : ℝ, 0 < eps → eps ≤ 1 →
          (M1avg eps G m hG).toENNReal <
            ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp 1 * (v+1) * (2 * Real.exp 1 / eps) ^ v)
  ```

  The passage of the proof:

  > By Theorem 18.4 in \cite{anthony1999neural}, if $\mathcal G$ is a nonempty class of functions from a set $X$ into $[0,1]$ with finite pseudo-dimension $v$, then for every $0<\epsilon\leqslant1$ and every positive integer $m$,
  > \begin{align*}
  > \mathcal{N}_{1}^{\mathrm{avg}}(\epsilon,\mathcal G,m)\leqslant\mathcal{M}_{1}^{\mathrm{avg}}(\epsilon,\mathcal G,m)<e(v+1)\left(\frac{2e}{\epsilon}\right)^{v},
  > \end{align*}
  > where $\mathcal{N}_{1}^{\mathrm{avg}}(\epsilon,\mathcal G,m)$ and $\mathcal{M}_{1}^{\mathrm{avg}}(\epsilon,\mathcal G,m)$ are the largest, over $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in X$, covering and packing numbers of $\{(g(x_1),\ldots,g(x_m)):g\in\mathcal G\}$ in the averaged metric $d_1(u,w)=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m|u_i-w_i|$.

Define \[ C_{\mathcal G}(L,K;\{d_i,n_i\})=\max\left\{A^{n_V},B\sum_{r=0}^{n_V-1}A^r\right\}. \] The identical intervention values contribute zero distance. Each component is compact because it is homeomorphic to a compact cube. Distinct components have positive distance because they are disjoint compact sets and there are finitely many of them. A sufficiently small neighborhood of a support point in $C_i$ meets no other component and has positive measure; hence $p_i>0$. If $d_i^C=0$, write $C_i=\{c_i\}$, use the unique map $\hat g_1^i:[0,1]\rightarrow[0,1]^0$, and set $\hat g_2^i=c_i$. This produces $\mu_i$ exactly.  For $q=d_i^C\geqslant1$, choose $g_2^i\in\mathcal H([0,1]^q,C_i)\cap\mathcal F_L([0,1]^q,C_i)$ from Assumption~\ref{assump:support}, and put $\nu_i=((g_2^i)^{-1})_{\#}\mu_i$. We instantiate Theorem VIII.1 of \cite{perekrestenkoHighDimensionalDistributionGeneration2022a} with its positive integer depth parameter $s=1$. For a refinement integer $n\geqslant2$, set \[ \delta=\frac{1}{\lceil\sqrt q(q+1)n(n-1)\rceil}. \] Since $\sqrt q(q+1)\geqslant2$, this choice satisfies \[ 0<\delta\leqslant\frac{1}{\sqrt q(q+1)n(n-1)}<\frac{1}{n(n-1)}. \] The quantization mesh in the cited theorem is $\delta/n$. Its conclusion supplies a one-input, $q$-output ReLU network $\Phi$ with at most $C_q(n^q+n^{q-1})$ nonzero weights and biases, depth $4q-2$ in the source's convention, and Euclidean Wasserstein error at most \[ \frac{\sqrt q}{2n}+\frac{2\sqrt q}{n}+\frac{q(q+1)}{2}(n-1)\delta \leqslant\frac{\sqrt q}{2n}+\frac{2\sqrt q}{n}+\frac{\sqrt q}{2n} =\frac{3\sqrt q}{n}. \] Here $C_q$ depends only on $q$. The pointwise inequality between the $1$-norm and the Euclidean norm multiplies this Wasserstein bound by at most $\sqrt q$, giving error at most $3q/n$ in the paper's norm.  A hidden unit with zero incoming weights and zero bias has identically zero output and can be deleted. After deleting these units, every remaining hidden unit accounts for a nonzero weight or bias, so every hidden layer has width at most $C_q(n^q+n^{q-1})\leqslant2C_qn^q$. Clip the output coordinates into $[0,1]$ using $t\mapsto\max\{t,0\}-\max\{t-1,0\}$. This requires width $2q$ and a fixed number of additional layers. Clipping fixes the target cube and is $1$-Lipschitz in the $1$-norm, so its application to the first marginal of any coupling cannot increase the error. There is consequently a constant $A_q\geqslant1$, depending only on $q$, such that the clipped network has width at most $A_qn^q$ and hidden depth $\Theta(q)$.  For every sufficiently large width budget, specifically $W_1\geqslant A_q2^q$, choose \[ n=\left\lfloor(W_1/A_q)^{1/q}\right\rfloor. \] Then $n\geqslant2$, $A_qn^q\leqslant W_1$, and $n\geqslant\tfrac12(W_1/A_q)^{1/q}$. With this choice the clipped network $\hat g_1^i$ satisfies \[ W(P(\hat g_1^i(U_i)),\nu_i)\leqslant\frac{3q}{n}\leqslant6qA_q^{1/q}W_1^{-1/q},\qquad U_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]). \] Thus the refinement integer increases with width, while the depth parameter stays equal to $1$; the mesh $\delta/n$ is $\Theta_q(W_1^{-3/q})$. Padding with zero units realizes width $W_1$ without altering the function.  For each scalar coordinate of $g_2^i$, apply Theorem 2(b) of \cite{Yarotsky2018OptimalAO} with positive input dimension $q$. It supplies width $2q+10$ and error bounded by a constant times the coordinate modulus of continuity at a constant times the number of weights raised to $-2/q$. At this fixed width the number of weights is proportional to depth. The Lipschitz modulus therefore gives coordinate error $O(L_2^{-2/q})$. Parallelizing the $d$ coordinate networks gives width $\Theta(dq)$ and a map $\hat g_2^i$ with $\\|g_2^i-\hat g_2^i\\|_\infty=O(L_2^{-2/q})$. Reserve a fixed number of layers for clipping into a box $[-B,B]^d$ containing all components; the remaining depth is proportional to $L_2$ for sufficiently large $L_2$, and clipping cannot increase any coordinate error. Lemma~\ref{lemma:push-forward_err} gives \[ W(\mu_i,P(\hat g_2^i\circ\hat g_1^i(U_i)))\leqslant L_iO(W_1^{-1/q})+d\,O(L_2^{-2/q})=O(W_1^{-1/q}+L_2^{-2/q}), \] where $L_i$ is the fixed chart Lipschitz constant.  Take independent uniform inputs $U_i$. Pad the first-block hidden depths to a common value $\Theta(D_C)$ and the second-block widths to $\Theta(dD_C)$. Identity layers on nonnegative hidden outputs preserve the maps. Let $\hat\mu_i=P(\hat g_2^i\circ\hat g_1^i(U_i))$. For budgets at least $1$, each positive $q\leqslant D_C$ satisfies $W_1^{-1/q}\leqslant W_1^{-1/D_C}$ and $L_2^{-2/q}\leqslant L_2^{-2/D_C}$. Singleton errors are zero. Lemma~\ref{lemma:combin_err} hence yields \[ W\left(\mathbb P,\sum_i p_i\hat\mu_i\right)\leqslant\sum_i p_iW(\mu_i,\hat\mu_i)\leqslant O\left(\mathbb I_{\{\max_i d_i^C>0\}}(W_1^{-1/D_C}+L_2^{-2/D_C})\right). \] Let $X^\tau$ be the Gumbel-softmax weights with probabilities $p_i$, independent of the block outputs, and let $X^0$ be their one-hot limit. The output with weights $X^0$ has law $\sum_i p_i\hat\mu_i$. Lemma~\ref{lemma:gumbel_err} gives $W(P(X^\tau),P(X^0))=O(\tau-\tau\log\tau)$ for $0<\tau<1$. Couple the weights and use identical independent block outputs $v_i$ in the two constructions. Since $\\|v_i\\|_\infty\leqslant B$, \[ \left\\|\sum_i(X_i^\tau-X_i^0)v_i\right\\|\leqslant\sum_i\|X_i^\tau-X_i^0\|\\|v_i\\|\leqslant dB\\|X^\tau-X^0\\|. \] Taking expectations and the infimum over weight couplings bounds the additional output Wasserstein error by $O(\tau-\tau\log\tau)$. The triangle inequality proves the stated estimate. If every component is a singleton, both deterministic blocks are exact and only the mixing error remains. · split off as results of their own: thm:cor-fix-3c402872 |

Independence of the original latent variables and independence of the chosen generator inputs allow application of \cref{lemma:product_err}, yielding \begin{align*} W(P(U_1,\ldots,U_{n_U}),P(\hat U_1,\ldots,\hat U_{n_U})) &\leqslant\sum_{j=1}^{n_U}W(P(U_j),P(\hat U_j))\\ &\leqslant O\left(L_1^{-2/d_{\max}^U}+L_2^{-2/d_{\max}^U}+(\tau-\tau\log\tau)\right). \end{align*} Indeed, for $d_j^U>0$, the inequalities $d_j^U\leqslant d_{\max}^U$ and $L_r\geqslant1$ give $L_r^{-2/d_j^U}\leqslant L_r^{-2/d_{\max}^U}$ for $r=1,2$, and there are only finitely many latent variables. Identical categorical Gumbel noises may be adjoined to both latent vectors without changing this bound: couple these noises identically for one inequality and project onto the non-Gumbel coordinates for the reverse inequality.       Let $ \hat{\mathcal{M}}$ be the casual model with the following structure equations      \begin{equation*} \hat{V}_{i} =\begin{cases} \hat{f}_{i}\left(\text{Pa} (\hat{V}_{i} ),(\hat{g}_{j} (Z_{C_{j}} ))_{U_{C_{j} }\in \boldsymbol{U}_{V_{i}}}\right), & V_{i}  \text{ is continuous} ,\\ \arg\max_{k\in [ n_{i}]}\left\{g_{k} +\log\left(\hat{f}_{i}\left(\text{Pa} (\hat{V}_{i} ),(\hat{g}_{j} (Z_{C_{j}} ))_{U_{C_{j} } \in \boldsymbol{U}_{V_{i}}}\right)  \right)_{k}\right\} , & V_{i}  \text{ is categorical} . \end{cases}  \end{equation*}       Replacing a categorical propensity vector $\hat f_i(x)$ by $\hat f_i(x)/\\|\hat f_i(x)\\|_1$ subtracts the same finite constant $\log\\|\hat f_i(x)\\|_1$ from every finite log propensity. It therefore preserves the categorical structural equation, with $\log0=-\infty$ for zero coordinates. Apply \cref{thm:approximation} to the globally $L$-Lipschitz true functions $\bar f_i$, the continuous approximate functions $\hat f_i$, and the normalized approximate categorical functions. The extended true model has boundedness constant $HB$ and, by the coupling induction in this proof, the same interventional laws as $\mathcal M^*$ for every intervention in the statement. Consequently, \begin{align*} &W\left(P^{\mathcal M^*}(\boldsymbol V(\boldsymbol t)),P^{\hat{\mathcal M}}(\boldsymbol V(\boldsymbol t))\right)\\ &\quad\leqslant C\left(\sum_{V_i\ \text{continuous}}\\|\bar f_i-\hat f_i\\|_\infty +\sum_{V_i\ \text{categorical}}\left\\|\bar f_i-\frac{\hat f_i}{\\|\hat f_i\\|_1}\right\\|_\infty +W(P(U_1,\ldots,U_{n_U}),P(\hat U_1,\ldots,\hat U_{n_U}))\right)\\ &\quad\leqslant O\left(L_0^{-2/d_{\max}^{\text{in}}}+L_1^{-2/d_{\max}^U}+L_2^{-2/d_{\max}^U}+(\tau-\tau\log\tau)\right). \end{align*} For the second inequality, every term of the first sum has the continuous structural error bound proved here, every term of the second sum has the normalized categorical error bound proved here, and the latent term has the bound obtained using \cref{lemma:product_err}; the two sums contain only finitely many nodes. Couple corresponding non-Gumbel latent laws optimally and take the product of these couplings, using their independence. The expected joint latent $1$-norm discrepancy is the sum of their marginal Wasserstein distances. Generate the observed nodes in a topological order. At a continuous node the expected output discrepancy is at most the structural output $1$-norm approximation error plus $\hat L_f$ times the expected input discrepancy. At a categorical node with conditional propensity vectors $p,p'$, a maximal coupling has disagreement probability $\\|p-p'\\|_1/2$; its expected label distance is at most $(n_i-1)\\|p-p'\\|_1/2$. Such a coupling assigns common mass $\min\{p_k,p'_k\}$ to label $k$ and distributes the remaining masses on the disjoint residual supports. It preserves each model's conditional categorical law. If $e$ is the sum of the expected latent and previously generated observed discrepancies, adjoining a continuous node increases it to at most $(1+\hat L_f)e+d_i\\|f_i-f'_i\\|_\infty$; adjoining a categorical node increases it to at most $(1+(n_i-1)\hat L_f/2)e+n_i(n_i-1)\\|f_i-f'_i\\|_\infty/2$. Choose fixed constants $A\geqslant1$ and $B$ bounding these finitely many coefficients. Iterating $e_{k+1}\leqslant Ae_k+Bd(\theta,\theta')$ gives \[ e_k\leqslant A^ke_0+Bd(\theta,\theta')\sum_{r=0}^{k-1}A^r. \] Indeed, the formula holds for $k=0$, and multiplying its right side by $A$ and adding $Bd(\theta,\theta')$ gives the formula for $k+1$. Identical intervention values contribute zero discrepancy and remove their generation steps. Projection to the observed coordinates therefore proves \[ W(P^\theta(\boldsymbol V(\boldsymbol t)),P^{\theta'}(\boldsymbol V(\boldsymbol t)))\leqslant C d(\theta,\theta') \] uniformly over the intervention values, with $C$ depending on the fixed graph, dimensions, cardinalities and regularity bounds. For fixed $n$, pad the finitely many network architectures to their stated widths and encode each representation by its finitely many real weights and mixture probabilities. Finite products of Euclidean spaces and simplices are standard Borel spaces. Affine maps, ReLU, clipping and finite composition have jointly continuous evaluation in their weights and inputs. At the fixed temperature $\tau_n>0$, mixture weights can be written \[ \frac{p_j^{1/\tau_n}\exp(G_j/\tau_n)}{\sum_k p_k^{1/\tau_n}\exp(G_k/\tau_n)},\qquad p\in\Delta, \] whose denominator is positive even when some $p_j=0$; hence generator evaluation is jointly Borel. Continuity makes the output bound, coordinatewise nonnegativity and every Lipschitz inequality equivalent to their inequalities on that dense set or its Cartesian square. Each such inequality is Borel in the weights. For a nonnegative categorical raw network $q$, positivity on a compact input box $D_0$ is equivalent to membership in \[ \bigcup_{l=1}^\infty\bigcap_{x\in Q_0}\{\eta:\\|q_\eta(x)\\|_1\geqslant1/l\}, \] where $Q_0$ is countable and dense in $D_0$; continuity and attainment of a minimum prove both implications. The exogenous input space is a finite product of uniform cubes and real Gumbel coordinates, hence standard Borel. The smallest minimizing label is $i$ exactly when $r_i<r_j$ for every $j<i$ and $r_i\leqslant r_j$ for every $j>i$; this is a finite intersection of Borel comparisons. For a parameter at an interval endpoint, both incident cubes contain the assigned value. For such a law $\mathbb P$, write its support components as $C_i=\{a_i\}$ and put $\mu_i=\mathbb P\|_{C_i}/\mathbb P(C_i)$. The map $f:[0,1]^0\rightarrow C_i$ sending the unique point to $a_i$ is a Lipschitz homeomorphism. Since $h(T)\geqslant0$ for every probability plan, \[ W_{1,\lambda}(\mu,\nu)\leqslant\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}T^*_{ij}-\lambda h(T^*)\leqslant W(\mu,\nu). \] Also $\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}(T_\lambda)_{ij}\geqslant W(\mu,\nu)$. It follows that \begin{align}\label{eq:err_reg_wass} -\lambda\max_{T\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}h(T)\leqslant W_{1,\lambda}(\mu,\nu)-W(\mu,\nu)\leqslant0. \end{align} Since $ T_{ij} \in [ 0,1]$ and $ f( x) =-x\log x$ is concave, we have  \begin{align*} h( T) = & -nm\cdot \frac{1}{nm}\sum _{i,j=1}^{n,m} T_{ij}\log T_{ij} +1.\\  & \leqslant -nm\cdot \left(\frac{1}{nm}\sum _{i,j=1}^{n,m} T_{ij}\right)\log\left(\frac{1}{nm}\sum _{i,j=1}^{n,m} T_{ij}\right) +1\\  & =1+\log( nm) . \end{align*} By definition of Sinkhorn distance,  \begin{align*} S_{\lambda }( \mu ,\nu ) & = W_{1,\lambda }( \mu ,\nu ) -W_{1,\lambda }( \mu ,\mu )/2 -W_{1,\lambda }( \nu ,\nu )/2 . \end{align*} Let $a=W_{1,\lambda}(\mu,\nu)-W(\mu,\nu)$, $b=W_{1,\lambda}(\mu,\mu)$, and $c=W_{1,\lambda}(\nu,\nu)$. The self-transport Wasserstein costs are zero. By (\ref{eq:err_reg_wass}) and the entropy calculation, \[ \|a\|\leqslant(1+\log(nm))\lambda,\quad \|b\|\leqslant(1+2\log n)\lambda,\quad \|c\|\leqslant(1+2\log m)\lambda. \] Consequently \begin{align*} \|S_\lambda(\mu,\nu)-W(\mu,\nu)\| &=\|a-b/2-c/2\|\\ &\leqslant\|a\|+\|b\|/2+\|c\|/2\\ &\leqslant2(1+\log(nm))\lambda. \end{align*} |

| statement | \label{lemma:sup_wasserstein} Given a measure $ \mu $ on $ \mathbb{R}^{d}$ and a real function class $ \mathcal{F}$ with output dimension $ d$, suppose that the pseudo-dimension of $ \mathcal{F}$ is less than $ d_{\mathcal{F}} < \infty $ and there exists $K>0$ such that $ \|f( x) \|\leqslant K,\forall f\in \mathcal{F} ,x\in \mathbb{R}^{d'}$, then with probability at least $ 1-\exp\left( O\left( \delta ^{-d}\log\left( \delta ^{-1}\right) +d_{\mathcal{F}}\log \epsilon ^{-1} -n\epsilon ^{2}\right)\right)$, \begin{align*} \sup _{f\in \mathcal{F}} W( f_{\#} \mu ,f_{\#} \mu _{n}) & \leqslant \delta +\epsilon \end{align*} for all $ \delta ,\epsilon >0$, where $ \mu _{n}$ is the empirical distribution of $ \mu $. |

| findings | [refuted, V1.5] the step its proof takes from [anthony1999neural, Theorems 18.4 and 17.1] (lem:sup-wasserstein-anthony-theorems) does not hold as the proof uses it: (a) For vector-valued $\mathcal F$, its pseudo-dimension could mean $\max_{j\in[d]}\operatorname{Pdim}(\{f_j:f\in\mathcal F\})$ or $\operatorname{Pdim}(\{(x,j)\mapsto f_j(x):f\in\mathcal F\})$. These impose different bounds, and neither the paper nor the scalar cited theorem specifies the choice. The dual formulation does determine that $h$ is scalar-valued. (b) The attributed covering inequality is false for the paper's explicitly unnormalized empirical $\ell_1$ metric: its bound omits sample-size scaling. (c) It also omits range scaling: Theorem 18.4 requires scalar functions valued in $[0,1]$, whereas the host only bounds their magnitude by arbitrary $K$. The fixed-$h$ concentration order can be recovered from Theorem 17.1 by range normalization and a square-root transformation with zero responses, but that does not validate the printed covering inequality. witness: (b) Take $d=d'=1$, $\mu=\mathrm{Unif}([-1,1])$, $K=1$, $h(x)=x$, and $\mathcal F=\{f_c:c\in[0,1/2]\}$, where $f_c(x)=c+\tfrac12\mathbb{I}_{x\geqslant0}$. This nonconstant class has pseudo-dimension $1$, so choose $d_{\mathcal F}=2$. Its evaluation vectors have distance $n\|c-c'\|$ in the printed metric. With $n=10000$ and $\epsilon=1/4$, every covering ball covers a parameter interval of length at most $2\epsilon/n$, so $\mathcal N_1(\epsilon,\mathcal F,n)\geqslant10000$. The asserted upper bound is $3e(8e)^2=192e^3<4000$, a contradiction. (c) Independently take $K=10000$, $n=2$, and $f_c(x)=c+(K/2)\mathbb{I}_{x\geqslant0}$ for $c\in[0,K/2]$, keeping the other choices. The host's hypotheses again hold with pseudo-dimension $1$. At $\epsilon=1/4$, its printed covering number is at least $20000$; even the averaged empirical metric gives a lower bound of $10000$. Both exceed the same asserted bound $192e^3$. Rescaling the range to $[0,1]$ changes the covering radius and introduces the omitted dependence on $K$. minimal patch (confirmed): corrected statement: Given a probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^{d'}$ and a class $\mathcal F$ of measurable functions $f:\mathbb R^{d'}\rightarrow\mathbb R^d$, suppose that each scalar coordinate class $\mathcal F_j=\{x\mapsto f_j(x):f\in\mathcal F\}$, $j\in[d]$, has pseudo-dimension less than $d_{\mathcal F}<\infty$ and there exists $K>0$ such that $\\|f(x)\\|_\infty\leqslant K$ for all $f\in\mathcal F$ and $x\in\mathbb R^{d'}$. Suppose in addition that there are a standard Borel space $T$ and a jointly Borel map $G:T\times\mathbb R^{d'}\rightarrow[-K,K]^d$ such that $\mathcal F=\{G(t,\cdot):t\in T\}$. There are positive constants $C,c$ depending only on $d,K$ such that, with probability at least \[ 1-\exp\left(C\left((1+\delta^{-d})\log(2+\delta^{-1})+d_{\mathcal F}\log(2+\epsilon^{-1})\right)-cn\epsilon^2\right), \] \begin{align*} \sup_{f\in\mathcal F}W(f_{\#}\mu,f_{\#}\mu_n)\leqslant\delta+\epsilon \end{align*} for all $\delta,\epsilon>0$, where $\mu_n$ is the empirical distribution of $\mu$. · proof change: The empty class satisfies the uniform assertion vacuously, so assume $T\ne\varnothing$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent observations with law $\mu$. By the dual formulation of Wasserstein distance, \begin{align*} \sup_{f\in\mathcal F}W(f_{\#}\mu,f_{\#}\mu_n) =\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\left(\mathbb E_{X\sim\mu_n}h(f(X))-\mathbb E_{X\sim\mu}h(f(X))\right), \end{align*} where \[ \mathcal H=\{h:[-K,K]^d\rightarrow\mathbb R:h(0)=0,\ \|h(x)-h(y)\|\leqslant\\|x-y\\|\}. \] Every such $h$ takes values in $[-dK,dK]$. Retain the unnormalized empirical covering number \begin{align*} \mathcal N_1(r,\mathcal F,N)=\sup_{x_1,\ldots,x_N}\mathcal N\left(r,\{(f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_N)):f\in\mathcal F\},\\|\cdotp\\|_1\right), \end{align*} where the $1$-norm on the evaluation vector sums over all sample points and output coordinates.  With the uniform norm, $\mathcal H$ is closed, uniformly bounded and equicontinuous on the compact cube, hence is a compact metric space by Arzela--Ascoli. Evaluation $(h,y)\mapsto h(y)$ is continuous: its increment is bounded by $\\|h-h'\\|_\infty+\\|y-y'\\|$. Consequently $(t,h,x)\mapsto h(G(t,x))$ is jointly Borel on $T\times\mathcal H\times\mathbb R^{d'}$. Its bounded population integral is Borel in $(t,h)$: this holds for indicators of measurable rectangles, is preserved by bounded monotone limits and linear combinations, and extends to bounded Borel functions by the monotone class theorem. Every strict deviation event is the projection of a Borel set from this standard Borel parameter space and is therefore analytic and universally measurable; weak supremum events are countable intersections of strict ones. The same reasoning applies to two samples and finite coordinate swaps. All probabilities below are thus defined in the completion of the sample law. Obviously, if $ h$ is 1-Lipschitz,  \begin{align*} \mathcal{N}_{1}( \epsilon ,h\circ \mathcal{F} ,n) & \leqslant \mathcal{N}_{1}( \epsilon ,\mathcal{F} ,n) . \end{align*} Put $v=\lfloor d_{\mathcal F}\rfloor$. Each coordinate class has pseudo-dimension at most $v$. Normalize its range by $f_j\mapsto(f_j+K)/(2K)$. Applying Theorem 18.4 of \cite{anthony1999neural} in its averaged empirical metric, and then undoing the normalization, bounds a scalar unnormalized cover of radius $r/(2d)$ on $N$ points by \[ e(v+1)\left(2+\frac{8eKdN}{r}\right)^v. \] The additional $2$ allows radii beyond the normalized unit range. Take the product of these $d$ covers. For every product ball meeting the evaluation vectors of $\mathcal F$, choose one such vector as its center. Two vectors in that product ball differ by at most $r/d$ in each scalar unnormalized metric, hence by at most $r$ in the summed vector metric. Thus \[ \mathcal N_1(r,\mathcal F,N)\leqslant\left[e(v+1)\left(2+\frac{8eKdN}{r}\right)^v\right]^d. \] This exhibits both sample-size and range scaling.  Fix $h\in\mathcal H$, and define \[ a_f(x)=\frac{h(f(x))+dK}{2dK},\qquad z_f(x)=\sqrt{a_f(x)}. \] Both functions take values in $[0,1]$. On $N$ points, the inequality $\|\sqrt a-\sqrt b\|\leqslant\sqrt{\|a-b\|}$ and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give \[ \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\|z_f(x_i)-z_g(x_i)\|\leqslant\left(\frac{1}{2dKN}\sum_{i=1}^N\\|f(x_i)-g(x_i)\\|\right)^{1/2}. \] Consequently an unnormalized vector cover of radius $2dKNr^2$ gives an averaged scalar cover of the class $\{z_f:f\in\mathcal F\}$ of radius $r$, whose cardinality is at most \[ \left[e(v+1)(2+4e/r^2)^v\right]^d. \] By Theorem 17.1 in \cite{anthony1999neural}, with its standing measurability condition, let $X$ and $T_0$ be standard Borel spaces, let $g:T_0\times X\rightarrow[0,1]$ be jointly Borel, and put $\mathcal G=\{g(t,\cdot):t\in T_0\}\ne\varnothing$. For every Borel probability distribution $P$ on $X\times[0,1]$, every $0<\zeta<1$ and every positive integer $m$, \[ P^m\left\{\text{some }t\in T_0\text{ has }\left\|\mathbb E_{(x,y)\sim P}(g(t,x)-y)^2-\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m(g(t,x_i)-y_i)^2\right\|\geqslant\zeta\right\} \leqslant4\mathcal N_1^{\mathrm{avg}}(\zeta/16,\mathcal G,2m)\exp(-\zeta^2m/32). \] Here the draws are independent, the probability is taken in the completed sample law, and $\mathcal N_1^{\mathrm{avg}}$ uses the averaged empirical metric. For the present class, $(t,x)\mapsto\sqrt{(h(G(t,x))+dK)/(2dK)}$ is jointly Borel, since $h$ is continuous and the square root is continuous on $[0,1]$. Its parameter space is the same standard Borel space $T$, and its constant-response input law is $\mu\otimes\delta_0$. Apply this form of Theorem 17.1 to the class with response identically zero. Its squared loss is $z_f^2=a_f$. For $0<\epsilon<2dK$, put $\eta=\epsilon/(2dK)$ and use the averaged cover at radius $\eta/16$ on $2n$ points. The theorem gives \[ \mathbb P\left(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\|(\mu_n-\mu)(h\circ f)\|>\epsilon\right) \leqslant4\left[e(v+1)(2+1024e/\eta^2)^v\right]^d\exp(-n\eta^2/32). \] Since $v\leqslant d_{\mathcal F}$ and $\log(v+1)\leqslant v$, the logarithm of the right-hand side is bounded by $C_0+C_1d_{\mathcal F}\log(2+\epsilon^{-1})-c_1n\epsilon^2$, with constants depending only on $d,K$. If $\epsilon\geqslant2dK$, the deviation is deterministically at most $2dK$, and the desired deviation bound is immediate. Let $\mathcal H_\delta$ be a finite $\delta/2$-net of $\mathcal H$ in the uniform norm. Such a net has \[ \log\|\mathcal H_\delta\|\leqslant C_2(1+\delta^{-d})\log(2+\delta^{-1}), \] where $C_2$ depends only on $d,K$. To see this, take a grid in $[-K,K]^d$ with $1$-norm mesh at most $\delta/8$ and at most $(1+C_3/\delta)^d$ points. Quantize the values of $h$ at these points into bins of width at most $\delta/8$ in $[-dK,dK]$. There are at most $2+C_4/\delta$ bins at each point. Choose one member of $\mathcal H$ from each nonempty quantization pattern. Two functions with the same pattern differ by at most $\delta/8$ at grid points and by at most $3\delta/8$ everywhere, using their Lipschitz bounds and a nearest grid point. These representatives form the required net. Counting patterns gives the displayed entropy bound. Apply the fixed-$h$ concentration bound to every $h\in\mathcal H_\delta$ and take a union bound. For $0<\epsilon<2dK$, after enlarging a constant depending only on $d,K$, \[ \mathbb P\left(\sup_{h\in\mathcal H_\delta,f\in\mathcal F}(\mu_n-\mu)(h\circ f)>\epsilon\right) \leqslant\exp\left(C\left((1+\delta^{-d})\log(2+\delta^{-1})+d_{\mathcal F}\log(2+\epsilon^{-1})\right)-cn\epsilon^2\right). \] For every $h\in\mathcal H$, choose $\tilde h\in\mathcal H_\delta$ with $\\|h-\tilde h\\|_\infty\leqslant\delta/2$. Since $\mu_n$ and $\mu$ are probability measures, \[ \|(\mu_n-\mu)((h-\tilde h)\circ f)\|\leqslant\delta. \] Therefore \[ \sup_{h\in\mathcal H,f\in\mathcal F}(\mu_n-\mu)(h\circ f) \leqslant\delta+\sup_{\tilde h\in\mathcal H_\delta,f\in\mathcal F}(\mu_n-\mu)(\tilde h\circ f). \] The dual formula yields the stated Wasserstein bound. If $\epsilon\geqslant2dK$, both push-forward measures are supported in a set of $1$-norm diameter $2dK$, so their Wasserstein distance is at most $2dK\leqslant\delta+\epsilon$ deterministically. This completes the proof for all positive $\delta,\epsilon$. |

At the first level, adjacency forces the four columns to be visited consecutively. At the second level, the four horizontal cells within each column must be visited vertically, in one of the two directions. At the third level, each such cell has four vertical-strip children, whose ordering must run horizontally from one extreme strip to the other. Across successive vertically adjacent second-level cells, these horizontal directions must alternate. Consequently, after four such cells, the first and last third-level cells within a first-level column lie on the same horizontal extreme. An interior first-level column must instead enter from one neighboring column and exit toward the other, requiring opposite extremes. This contradiction rules out the asserted orderings.

A bound using $1+KL$ can close this categorical step, but does not justify the printed coefficient. Zero propensities could alternatively be excluded or interpreted through an extended logarithm; the closed-simplex canonical convention determines the latter.

### `thm:wide-nn` (`Approximation.tex:462-474`)

- as printed: \label{thm:wide_nn} Given any probability measure $ \mathbb{P}$ on $ \mathbb{R}^{d}$ that satisfies \cref{assump:support}, let $ \lambda $ be the Lebesgue measure on $ [ 0,1]^{N_{C}}$, where $N_C$ is defined in \cref{assump:support}. \begin{enumerate} \item There exists a neural network $ \hat{g} \in \mathcal{NN}(W_1,\Theta(\max_j d_j^C),\Theta(d\cdot\max_j d_j^C),L_2,\tau)$ with the above architecture (\cref{fig:wide_nn}) such that \begin{equation*} W(\hat{g}_{\#} \lambda ,\mathbb{P}) \leqslant O\left( W_{1}^{-1/\max_i\{d_i^C\}} +L_{2}^{-2/\max_i\{d_i^C\}} +(\tau - \tau\log\tau) \right) . \end{equation*} \item Furthermore, if in addition, $ \mathbb{P}$ constrained to each component satisfies \cref{assumption:lower_bound}, there exists a neural network $ \hat{g} \in \mathcal{NN}(\Theta(\max_j d_j^C),L_1,\Theta(d\cdot\max_j d_j^C),L_2,\tau)$ with the above architecture such that \begin{equation*} W(\hat{g}_{\#} \lambda ,\mathbb{P}) \leqslant O\left( L_{1}^{-2/\max_i\{d_i^C\}} +L_{2}^{-2/\max_i\{d_i^C\}}+(\tau - \tau\log\tau)\right). \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}
- corrected: Given any probability measure $\mathbb P$ on $\mathbb R^d$ that satisfies \cref{assump:support}, let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]^{N_C}$, where $N_C$ is defined in \cref{assump:support}. Write $D_C=\max\{1,\max_i d_i^C\}$. \begin{enumerate} \item There exists a neural network $\hat g\in\mathcal{NN}(W_1,\Theta(D_C),\Theta(d\cdot D_C),L_2,\tau)$ with the above architecture (\cref{fig:wide_nn}) such that \begin{equation*} W(\hat g_{\#}\lambda,\mathbb P)\leqslant O\left(\mathbb I_{\{\max_i d_i^C>0\}}\left(W_1^{-1/D_C}+L_2^{-2/D_C}\right)+(\tau-\tau\log\tau)\right). \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}

- proof change: Put $p_i=\mathbb P(C_i)$ and $\mu_i=\mathbb P|_{C_i}/p_i$. Each component is compact because it is homeomorphic to a compact cube. Distinct components have positive distance because they are disjoint compact sets and there are finitely many of them. A sufficiently small neighborhood of a support point in $C_i$ meets no other component and has positive measure; hence $p_i>0$. If $d_i^C=0$, write $C_i=\{c_i\}$, use the unique map $\hat g_1^i:[0,1]\rightarrow[0,1]^0$, and set $\hat g_2^i=c_i$. This produces $\mu_i$ exactly.  For $q=d_i^C\geqslant1$, choose $g_2^i\in\mathcal H([0,1]^q,C_i)\cap\mathcal F_L([0,1]^q,C_i)$ from Assumption~\ref{assump:support}, and put $\nu_i=((g_2^i)^{-1})_{\#}\mu_i$. We instantiate Theorem VIII.1 of \cite{perekrestenkoHighDimensionalDistributionGeneration2022a} with its positive integer depth parameter $s=1$. For a refinement integer $n\geqslant2$, set \[ \delta=\frac{1}{\lceil\sqrt q(q+1)n(n-1)\rceil}. \] Since $\sqrt q(q+1)\geqslant2$, this choice satisfies \[ 0<\delta\leqslant\frac{1}{\sqrt q(q+1)n(n-1)}<\frac{1}{n(n-1)}. \] The quantization mesh in the cited theorem is $\delta/n$. Its conclusion supplies a one-input, $q$-output ReLU network $\Phi$ with at most $C_q(n^q+n^{q-1})$ nonzero weights and biases, depth $4q-2$ in the source's convention, and Euclidean Wasserstein error at most \[ \frac{\sqrt q}{2n}+\frac{2\sqrt q}{n}+\frac{q(q+1)}{2}(n-1)\delta \leqslant\frac{\sqrt q}{2n}+\frac{2\sqrt q}{n}+\frac{\sqrt q}{2n} =\frac{3\sqrt q}{n}. \] Here $C_q$ depends only on $q$. The pointwise inequality between the $1$-norm and the Euclidean norm multiplies this Wasserstein bound by at most $\sqrt q$, giving error at most $3q/n$ in the paper's norm.  A hidden unit with zero incoming weights and zero bias has identically zero output and can be deleted. After deleting these units, every remaining hidden unit accounts for a nonzero weight or bias, so every hidden layer has width at most $C_q(n^q+n^{q-1})\leqslant2C_qn^q$. Clip the output coordinates into $[0,1]$ using $t\mapsto\max\{t,0\}-\max\{t-1,0\}$. This requires width $2q$ and a fixed number of additional layers. Clipping fixes the target cube and is $1$-Lipschitz in the $1$-norm, so its application to the first marginal of any coupling cannot increase the error. There is consequently a constant $A_q\geqslant1$, depending only on $q$, such that the clipped network has width at most $A_qn^q$ and hidden depth $\Theta(q)$.  For every sufficiently large width budget, specifically $W_1\geqslant A_q2^q$, choose \[ n=\left\lfloor(W_1/A_q)^{1/q}\right\rfloor. \] Then $n\geqslant2$, $A_qn^q\leqslant W_1$, and $n\geqslant\tfrac12(W_1/A_q)^{1/q}$. With this choice the clipped network $\hat g_1^i$ satisfies \[ W(P(\hat g_1^i(U_i)),\nu_i)\leqslant\frac{3q}{n}\leqslant6qA_q^{1/q}W_1^{-1/q},\qquad U_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]). \] Thus the refinement integer increases with width, while the depth parameter stays equal to $1$; the mesh $\delta/n$ is $\Theta_q(W_1^{-3/q})$. Padding with zero units realizes width $W_1$ without altering the function.  For each scalar coordinate of $g_2^i$, apply Theorem 2(b) of \cite{Yarotsky2018OptimalAO} with positive input dimension $q$. It supplies width $2q+10$ and error bounded by a constant times the coordinate modulus of continuity at a constant times the number of weights raised to $-2/q$. At this fixed width the number of weights is proportional to depth. The Lipschitz modulus therefore gives coordinate error $O(L_2^{-2/q})$. Parallelizing the $d$ coordinate networks gives width $\Theta(dq)$ and a map $\hat g_2^i$ with $\|g_2^i-\hat g_2^i\|_\infty=O(L_2^{-2/q})$. Reserve a fixed number of layers for clipping into a box $[-B,B]^d$ containing all components; the remaining depth is proportional to $L_2$ for sufficiently large $L_2$, and clipping cannot increase any coordinate error. Lemma~\ref{lemma:push-forward_err} gives \[ W(\mu_i,P(\hat g_2^i\circ\hat g_1^i(U_i)))\leqslant L_iO(W_1^{-1/q})+d\,O(L_2^{-2/q})=O(W_1^{-1/q}+L_2^{-2/q}), \] where $L_i$ is the fixed chart Lipschitz constant.  Take independent uniform inputs $U_i$. Pad the first-block hidden depths to a common value $\Theta(D_C)$ and the second-block widths to $\Theta(dD_C)$. Identity layers on nonnegative hidden outputs preserve the maps. Let $\hat\mu_i=P(\hat g_2^i\circ\hat g_1^i(U_i))$. For budgets at least $1$, each positive $q\leqslant D_C$ satisfies $W_1^{-1/q}\leqslant W_1^{-1/D_C}$ and $L_2^{-2/q}\leqslant L_2^{-2/D_C}$. Singleton errors are zero. Lemma~\ref{lemma:combin_err} hence yields \[ W\left(\mathbb P,\sum_i p_i\hat\mu_i\right)\leqslant\sum_i p_iW(\mu_i,\hat\mu_i)\leqslant O\left(\mathbb I_{\{\max_i d_i^C>0\}}(W_1^{-1/D_C}+L_2^{-2/D_C})\right). \] Let $X^\tau$ be the Gumbel-softmax weights with probabilities $p_i$, independent of the block outputs, and let $X^0$ be their one-hot limit. The output with weights $X^0$ has law $\sum_i p_i\hat\mu_i$. Lemma~\ref{lemma:gumbel_err} gives $W(P(X^\tau),P(X^0))=O(\tau-\tau\log\tau)$ for $0<\tau<1$. Couple the weights and use identical independent block outputs $v_i$ in the two constructions. Since $\|v_i\|_\infty\leqslant B$, \[ \left\|\sum_i(X_i^\tau-X_i^0)v_i\right\|\leqslant\sum_i|X_i^\tau-X_i^0|\|v_i\|\leqslant dB\|X^\tau-X^0\|. \] Taking expectations and the infimum over weight couplings bounds the additional output Wasserstein error by $O(\tau-\tau\log\tau)$. The triangle inequality proves the stated estimate. If every component is a singleton, both deterministic blocks are exact and only the mixing error remains.
- why: the step its proof takes from [Yarotsky2018OptimalAO, Theorem 2] (lem:wide-nn-yarotsky-theorem-2) does not hold as the proof uses it: For $d_i^C\geqslant1$, the citation is valid: Theorem 2(b) supplies width $2d_i^C+10$, its weight count is proportional to $L_2$ for fixed dimension, and the Lipschitz modulus gives the asserted rate. However, the host permits $d_i^C=0$ and applies the citation to every component without establishing the source's positive input dimension. The source gives neither the displayed exponent nor the claimed width in that case.

Let $ d_{\max}^{\text{in}} $ and $d_{\max}^{\text{out}}$ be the largest input and output dimension of $f_i$ in (\ref{eq:structure_equation}) and $d_{\max}^U$ be the largest dimension of all latent variables. There exists a neural causal model $$\hat{\mathcal{M}} \in \text{NCM}_{\mathcal{G}} ( \mathcal{NN}(\Theta( d^{\text{in}}_{\max}d^{\text{out}}_{\max}) ,L_{0}) , \mathcal{NN}(\Theta(d_{\max}^U),L_1,\Theta((d_{\max}^U)^2),L_2))$$ with structure equations (\ref{eq:structure_equation_hat}). For any intervention $\boldsymbol{T} = \boldsymbol{t}$, $\hat{\mathcal{M}}$ satisfies \begin{equation*} W\left( P^{\mathcal{M}^*}(\boldsymbol{V}(\boldsymbol{t})),P^{\hat{\mathcal{M}}}(\boldsymbol{V}(\boldsymbol{t}))\right) \leqslant O(L_{0}^{-2/d^\text{in}_{\max}} +L_{1}^{-2/d^U_{\max}} +L_{2}^{-2/d^U_{\max}} +(\tau - \tau\log\tau) ). \end{equation*}

Standard graph terminology and the settled meaning of the component symbol fix distinct pairs and inclusion maximality.
- side condition added by the confirming referee `ass:pin-181`: Writing $x=(\text{Pa}(V_i),\boldsymbol{U}_{V_i})$, the displayed law means $P(V_i=k\mid x)=(f_i(x))_k/\|f_i(x)\|_1$ for the nonnegative weight vector defining the categorical distribution, with zero coordinates interpreted using $\log 0=-\infty$. — pins reading of ass:assump-categorical-rv-generation: The paragraph introducing Assumption \ref{assump:categorical_rv} separates shared inputs influencing propensity functions from independent categorical-generation noise. Assumption \ref{assump:Lip_and_bounded} explicitly identifies normalized propensity coordinates with conditional category probabilities.
- side condition added by the confirming referee `ass:pin-182`: For categorical $V_i$, $f_i(x)=(\mathbb{P}(V_i=j\mid x))_{j\in[n_i]}$ is the structural propensity vector, and $\|f_i(x)-f_i(x')\|\leqslant L_f\|x-x'\|$ on its structural input domain, using the paper's $1$-norm. — pins reading of ass:assump-lip-and-bounded-categorical: Equation (\ref{eq:structure_equation}) uses $f_i$ as a normalized vector with indexed coordinates, while the notation paragraph defines the unadorned norm as the $1$-norm. The assumption applies Lipschitz continuity to that same $f_i$.
- side condition added by the confirming referee `ass:pin-183`: There is a deterministic $K>0$ such that $\max_{i\in[n_V],j\in[n_U]}\{\|V_i\|_\infty,\|U_j\|_\infty\}\leqslant K$ almost surely under the SCM law. — pins reading of ass:assump-lip-and-bounded-bound: Assumption \ref{assump:Lip_and_bounded} bounds the model-generated random variables themselves, and the surrounding setup treats their probability laws as the objects of comparison. It does not quantify over exceptional realizations of a probability-space representation.
- side condition added by the confirming referee `ass:pin-186`: The phrase ``uniform cubes'' denotes the unit cube domains $[0,1]^m$ used for deterministic uniform function approximation; it imposes no uniform probability law on structural inputs. — pins reading of ass:relu-approximation-domain: The same paragraph displays approximation of functions on $[0,1]^{d_1}$ and separately says that similar arguments apply to any bounded cubes.
- side condition added by the confirming referee `ass:pin-189`: For distinct observed vertices $V_i,V_j$, the ``correlated latent variable pair'' criterion means that some $U_k\in\boldsymbol{U}_{V_i}$ and $U_l\in\boldsymbol{U}_{V_j}$ are not independent, with $k=l$ permitted. — pins reading of def:eq-structure-eq: The paragraph immediately preceding Assumption \ref{assump:independence_u} explains that latent variables may enter several equations and that, under independence of the indexed latent family, a bidirected arrow represents a common latent parent. No covariance or moment convention is imposed in the SCM definition.
- side condition added by the confirming referee `ass:pin-190`: In the categorical branch of (\ref{eq:structure_equation}), zero coordinates of the normalized nonnegative vector $f_i(x)$ are allowed and are evaluated using $\log 0=-\infty$. — pins reading of def:eq-structure-equation: The canonical definition normalizes categorical propensity vectors, and Assumption \ref{assump:Lip_and_bounded} identifies their coordinates with conditional probabilities. The probability-simplex convention permits zero probabilities, so strict positivity would impose an additional restriction.
- side condition added by the confirming referee `ass:pin-191`: Under $\boldsymbol{T}=\boldsymbol{t}$, every unreplaced equation is evaluated in topological order at the intervened values of its parents, with the original latent law unchanged; for canonical categorical nodes the unreplaced equation is the categorical branch of (\ref{eq:structure_equation}). — pins reading of def:intervention: The intervention passage explicitly calls these the structural equations of the intervened model and defines the resulting variables as their values under intervention. The later canonical definition specifies the categorical form of those structural equations.
- side condition added by the confirming referee `ass:pin-192`: A network in $\mathcal{NN}_{k_1,k_2}(W,L)$ has $L$ hidden ReLU layers of width at most $W$, followed by an affine output layer of dimension $k_2$. — pins reading of def:relu-networks: The owner's binding convention in ass:pin-owner-3 explicitly fixes the layer count and hidden-layer widths.

- side condition added by the confirming referee `ass:pin-199`: $d_{\max}^U=\max_{j\in[n_U]}d_j^U$ ranges over non-Gumbel latent variables, while $d_{\max}^{\mathrm{in}}=\max_i d_i^{\mathrm{in}}$ and $d_{\max}^{\mathrm{out}}=\max_i d_i^{\mathrm{out}}$, with $d_i^{\mathrm{out}}=n_i$ for categorical nodes. — pins reading of def:corollary-deep-nn-dimensions: The NCM construction separately approximates non-Gumbel latent distributions and the functions in the canonical structural equations; those functions output categorical propensity vectors. - proof change: the printed proof, revised step by step] Suppose that structure equations of $ \mathcal{M}$ are     \begin{equation*} V_{i} =\begin{cases} f_{i}\left(\text{Pa} (V_{i} ),\boldsymbol{U}_{V_{i}}\right) , & V_{i} \ \text{is continuous} ,\\ \arg\max_{k\in [ n_{i}]}\left\{g_{k}^{V_{i}} +\log\left( f_{i}\left(\text{Pa}( V_{i}) ,\boldsymbol{U}_{V_{i}}\right)\right)_{k}\right\} , & V_{i} \ \text{is categorical} , \|f_i\|_1=  1 \end{cases}, \quad f_{i} \in \mathcal{F}_L.  \end{equation*}       Put $m_i=d_i^{\text{in}}$, let $d_i^{\text{out}}$ be the output dimension of $f_i$, and put $m=d_{\max}^{\text{in}}>0$. In each structural input, distinguish the real coordinates, consisting of continuous parents and non-Gumbel latent coordinates, from the categorical parent coordinates. Let $a_i$ have value zero in every real coordinate and value one in every categorical coordinate. Define the fixed constants \[ B_0=\max\left(\{1,R,K\}\cup\{n_i:V_i\text{ is categorical}\}\cup\{\|f_i(a_i)\|_\infty:V_i\text{ is continuous}\}\right),\qquad H=1+2Lm,\qquad B=B_0H^{n_V}. \] These constants do not depend on the intervention or on the network budgets.  We first bound all true structural inputs for the interventions in the statement. Work on the probability-one event where every non-Gumbel latent coordinate has absolute value at most $K$. Order the observed nodes topologically. We claim that the node in position $\ell$ has infinity norm at most $B_0H^\ell$. An intervened continuous node has norm at most $R\leqslant B_0$, and a categorical node has value at most its cardinality, which is at most $B_0$. For a nonintervened continuous node in position $\ell$, the induction hypothesis bounds all its parents and latent coordinates by $b=B_0H^{\ell-1}$. Every coordinate of $a_i$ has absolute value at most one, so its actual input $x_i$ satisfies $\|x_i-a_i\|\leqslant2m_i b\leqslant2mb$. Consequently, \[ \|f_i(x_i)\|_\infty\leqslant\|f_i(a_i)\|_\infty+L\|x_i-a_i\|\leqslant B_0+2Lmb\leqslant Hb=B_0H^\ell. \] This proves the induction, including its first position. In particular, every true structural input belongs to $Q_i=[-B,B]^{m_i}$, simultaneously for all permitted interventions. For $m_i=0$, interpret $Q_i$ as the unique point of $\mathbb R^0$.  We next define a Lipschitz extension to real values of the categorical input coordinates. A categorical input coordinate with only one category is always replaced by one. For each remaining categorical input coordinate $r$, with category count $c_r\geqslant2$, clip its value $x_r$ to $t_r\in[1,c_r]$, and set \[ k_r=\min\{c_r-1,\lfloor t_r\rfloor\},\qquad \theta_r=t_r-k_r\in[0,1]. \] Let $s_i$ be the number of these remaining categorical coordinates. For $\beta\in\{0,1\}^{s_i}$, let $x^\beta$ retain the real coordinates of $x$, replace coordinate $r$ by $k_r+\beta_r$, and replace every one-category coordinate by one. With $w_{r,0}=1-\theta_r$ and $w_{r,1}=\theta_r$, define \[ f_i^\dagger(x)=\sum_{\beta\in\{0,1\}^{s_i}}\left(\prod_{r=1}^{s_i}w_{r,\beta_r}\right)f_i(x^\beta). \] When $s_i=0$, the sum has one term with weight one. Thus this definition includes functions with no categorical parents. At valid categorical labels it agrees with $f_i$.  This interpolation preserves the $L$-Lipschitz bound in the paper's $1$-norm. Changing one real coordinate leaves the interpolation weights fixed, so the difference is a convex combination of differences bounded in $1$-norm by $L$ times the coordinate change. With all other coordinates fixed, on each interval between consecutive labels a categorical coordinate gives a linear interpolation between two vectors whose $1$-norm difference is at most $L$. Its slope therefore has $1$-norm at most $L$; outside the label interval the function is constant in that coordinate. Splitting any coordinate change at its finitely many intervening labels proves the same bound for an arbitrary change of that coordinate. Changing all coordinates one at a time and adding the bounds gives \[ \|f_i^\dagger(x)-f_i^\dagger(y)\|\leqslant L\|x-y\|. \] For a categorical output, the interpolation weights are nonnegative and sum to one, so $f_i^\dagger(x)\in\Delta_{n_i}$ for every real input $x$.  Let $\Pi_i:\mathbb R^{m_i}\to Q_i$ be coordinatewise projection, explicitly \[ (\Pi_i x)_r=-B+\max\{x_r+B,0\}-\max\{x_r-B,0\}, \] and define $\bar f_i=f_i^\dagger\circ\Pi_i$. Clipping each coordinate cannot increase its distance from another clipped coordinate; summing proves $\|\Pi_i x-\Pi_i y\|\leqslant\|x-y\|$. Hence $\bar f_i$ is globally $L$-Lipschitz. Since $a_i\in Q_i$, for every $z\in Q_i$ and every continuous output, \[ \|f_i^\dagger(z)\|_\infty\leqslant\|f_i(a_i)\|_\infty+L\|z-a_i\|\leqslant B_0+2LmB\leqslant HB. \] Thus $\bar f_i$ is globally bounded by $HB$ for continuous outputs; categorical outputs remain probability vectors.  Use the same latent laws and Gumbel noises to form the model with structural functions $\bar f_i$. Couple it with the original model using identical draws. Intervened nodes agree by their assigned values. If the parents of a nonintervened node agree, their common original input belongs to $Q_i$ and has valid categorical coordinates. Projection fixes this input and interpolation agrees there with $f_i$, so the structural outputs agree; for a categorical node use the identical Gumbel draws and the convention $\log0=-\infty$. Induction in topological order proves equality of the two interventional laws for every intervention in the statement. The extended true model satisfies the boundedness assumption with the fixed enlarged constant $HB$, because its nonintervened continuous outputs are globally bounded by $HB$, its categorical labels are at most $B_0$, its assigned treatment coordinates are at most $B_0$, and its non-Gumbel latent coordinates are at most $B_0$.  We now choose the neural approximants in place of the exact-minimizer construction. Reserve $c=4$ hidden layers of the structural budget for projection, categorical floors, and padding. For each $m_i>0$, apply \cite[Theorem 2]{Yarotsky2018OptimalAO}, part b), to every coordinate of $f_i^\dagger$ on $Q_i$, after the affine rescaling $z\mapsto2Bz-B\boldsymbol 1$ from $[0,1]^{m_i}$. The rescaled coordinate functions have Lipschitz moduli bounded by a fixed constant times their argument. The source gives scalar width $2m_i+10$ and error at most a fixed constant times the modulus at a constant times the number of weights raised to $-2/m_i$. At fixed width that number is proportional to hidden depth. Parallelizing the $d_i^{\text{out}}$ coordinates therefore gives, for every sufficiently large $L_0$, a network $q_i$ of width at most $d_i^{\text{out}}(2m_i+10)$ and hidden depth at most $L_0-c$ such that \[ \sup_{z\in Q_i}\|q_i(z)-f_i^\dagger(z)\|_\infty\leqslant C_i(L_0-c)^{-2/m_i}. \] The constant $C_i$ is fixed independently of $L_0$. For $L_0\geqslant2c$, choose a fixed $A_i\geqslant\max\{1,2^{2/m_i}C_i\}$ and set \[ \epsilon_i=A_iL_0^{-2/m_i}. \] Then choose one of the networks just supplied, so that its uniform error on $Q_i$ is at most $\epsilon_i$. Define the structural networks by \[ \hat f_i(x)= \begin{cases} q_i(\Pi_i x),&V_i\text{ is continuous},\\ \bigl(\max\{\epsilon_i,(q_i(\Pi_i x))_k\}\bigr)_{k=1}^{n_i},&V_i\text{ is categorical}. \end{cases} \] For $m_i=0$, instead set $\epsilon_i=0$ and let $\hat f_i=f_i$ be the exact constant affine network. These definitions specify $\hat f_i$ without any choice of a minimizer.  Projection uses one hidden layer with at most $2m_i$ units, and each categorical floor is $z\mapsto\epsilon_i+\max\{z-\epsilon_i,0\}$, using one further hidden layer. Affine maps between these layers and the network $q_i$ are absorbed into the adjacent affine transformations. If signed coordinates must be carried through a hidden layer, use $z=\max\{z,0\}-\max\{-z,0\}$ with two units per coordinate. Thus the reserved four layers suffice, with width at most $4m_i+2d_i^{\text{out}}(2m_i+10)+2d_i^{\text{out}}$. For $m_i\geqslant1$ and $d_i^{\text{out}}\geqslant1$, this is at most $30m_i d_i^{\text{out}}\leqslant64d_{\max}^{\text{in}}d_{\max}^{\text{out}}$, because $2m_i+10\leqslant12m_i$. A constant map with $m_i=0$ uses at most $2d_i^{\text{out}}$ units per hidden layer by carrying its positive and negative parts, which also fits this universal width since $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}\geqslant1$. A zero-dimensional output needs no units. Zero padding of units and insertion of identity layers on nonnegative hidden outputs give the structural architecture and hidden depth $L_0$ in the statement.  The continuous global approximation error is at most $\epsilon_i$, because $\Pi_i x\in Q_i$ for every input $x$. For categorical outputs, if $p\geqslant0$ and $\epsilon\geqslant0$, then \[ |\max\{\epsilon,z\}-p|\leqslant\max\{\epsilon,|z-p|\}. \] Indeed, for $z\geqslant\epsilon$ the left side is $|z-p|$; for $z<\epsilon$ and $p\leqslant\epsilon$ it is at most $\epsilon$; and for $z<\epsilon<p$ it is $p-\epsilon\leqslant p-z$. Apply this inequality coordinatewise at $\Pi_i x$ to obtain \[ \sup_{x\in\mathbb R^{m_i}}\|\hat f_i(x)-\bar f_i(x)\|_\infty\leqslant\epsilon_i. \] For $m_i>0$, every categorical coordinate is at least $\epsilon_i>0$. For $m_i=0$, the exact constant vector is a probability vector. In both cases its $1$-norm is strictly positive. The global error bound holds also when generated latent or parent inputs lie outside $Q_i$.              For a categorical variable, at an arbitrary input $x$, put $p=\bar f_i(x)$, $q=\hat f_i(x)$, $a=\|q\|_1$, and $S=\|q-p\|_\infty$. The construction gives $a>0$ and $S\leqslant\epsilon_i$. Since $p$ is a probability vector and $q$ is nonnegative, \[ |a-1|\leqslant\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}|q_j-p_j|\leqslant n_iS. \] For sufficiently large $L_0$, simultaneously for all nodes with $m_i>0$, we have $n_i\epsilon_i\leqslant1/2$, and hence $a\geqslant1/2$. Since $\|p\|_\infty\leqslant1$, \begin{align*} \left\|\frac q a-p\right\|_\infty &\leqslant\frac{\|q-p\|_\infty+|1-a|\|p\|_\infty}{a}\\ &\leqslant2(n_i+1)S\leqslant2(n_i+1)\epsilon_i. \end{align*} For $m_i=0$, normalization is exact because $q=p$ and $a=1$. For $m_i>0$, the inequalities $m_i\leqslant d_{\max}^{\text{in}}$ and $L_0\geqslant1$ imply $L_0^{-2/m_i}\leqslant L_0^{-2/d_{\max}^{\text{in}}}$. Taking the supremum over every real structural input therefore gives \[ \left\|\bar f_i-\frac{\hat f_i}{\|\hat f_i\|_1}\right\|_\infty\leqslant O(L_0^{-2/d_{\max}^{\text{in}}}). \] The continuous structural error has the same order without normalization. These bounds use the fixed cardinalities $n_i$ and do not require $n_i\leqslant K$. For each non-Gumbel latent variable $U_j$ with positive dimension $d_j^U$, apply the proposition entitled ``Deep distribution approximation'' to its law. Choose the resulting generators with independent uniform and Gumbel inputs $Z_j$ and put $\hat U_j=\hat g_j(Z_j)$. Each component cube dimension is at most the ambient dimension $d_j^U$. For budgets at least one, the component bounds therefore give \[ W(P(U_j),P(\hat U_j))\leqslant O\left(L_1^{-2/d_j^U}+L_2^{-2/d_j^U}+(\tau-\tau\log\tau)\right). \] For a component of positive cube dimension $q\leqslant d_j^U$, the scalar first-block networks have width $12$, and the scalar second-block networks have width $2q+10\leqslant12q$. Parallelization gives widths $12q$ and $12d_j^Uq$. Coordinate clipping needs at most $2q$ or $2d_j^U$ units, and carrying signed values requires at most twice the corresponding width; reserving four layers therefore gives widths at most $64q$ and $64d_j^Uq$. A singleton component uses its exact constant blocks; carrying a signed constant second-block output needs at most $2d_j^U$ units. Since $d_{\max}^U\geqslant1$, every component fits widths $64d_{\max}^U$ and $64(d_{\max}^U)^2$. These are the per-component widths in the separable architecture, so the number of components does not multiply either width budget. Zero padding and identity layers on nonnegative hidden outputs give the architecture in the statement. The numerical factor $64$ is independent of the model, $R$, dimensions, and cardinalities; only the error constants and minimum depth budgets may depend on the fixed model. A latent vector of dimension zero is the unique point of $\mathbb R^0$ and is represented exactly, with error zero. Independence of the original latent variables and independence of the chosen generator inputs allow application of \cref{lemma:product_err}, yielding \begin{align*} W(P(U_1,\ldots,U_{n_U}),P(\hat U_1,\ldots,\hat U_{n_U})) &\leqslant\sum_{j=1}^{n_U}W(P(U_j),P(\hat U_j))\\ &\leqslant O\left(L_1^{-2/d_{\max}^U}+L_2^{-2/d_{\max}^U}+(\tau-\tau\log\tau)\right). \end{align*} Indeed, for $d_j^U>0$, the inequalities $d_j^U\leqslant d_{\max}^U$ and $L_r\geqslant1$ give $L_r^{-2/d_j^U}\leqslant L_r^{-2/d_{\max}^U}$ for $r=1,2$, and there are only finitely many latent variables. Identical categorical Gumbel noises may be adjoined to both latent vectors without changing this bound: couple these noises identically for one inequality and project onto the non-Gumbel coordinates for the reverse inequality.       Let $ \hat{\mathcal{M}}$ be the casual model with the following structure equations      \begin{equation*} \hat{V}_{i} =\begin{cases} \hat{f}_{i}\left(\text{Pa} (\hat{V}_{i} ),(\hat{g}_{j} (Z_{C_{j}} ))_{U_{C_{j} }\in \boldsymbol{U}_{V_{i}}}\right), & V_{i}  \text{ is continuous} ,\\ \arg\max_{k\in [ n_{i}]}\left\{g_{k} +\log\left(\hat{f}_{i}\left(\text{Pa} (\hat{V}_{i} ),(\hat{g}_{j} (Z_{C_{j}} ))_{U_{C_{j} } \in \boldsymbol{U}_{V_{i}}}\right)  \right)_{k}\right\} , & V_{i}  \text{ is categorical} . \end{cases}  \end{equation*}       Replacing a categorical propensity vector $\hat f_i(x)$ by $\hat f_i(x)/\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1$ subtracts the same finite constant $\log\|\hat f_i(x)\|_1$ from every finite log propensity. It therefore preserves the categorical structural equation, with $\log0=-\infty$ for zero coordinates. Apply \cref{thm:approximation} to the globally $L$-Lipschitz true functions $\bar f_i$, the continuous approximate functions $\hat f_i$, and the normalized approximate categorical functions. The extended true model has boundedness constant $HB$ and, by the coupling induction in this proof, the same interventional laws as $\mathcal M^*$ for every intervention in the statement. Consequently, \begin{align*} &W\left(P^{\mathcal M^*}(\boldsymbol V(\boldsymbol t)),P^{\hat{\mathcal M}}(\boldsymbol V(\boldsymbol t))\right)\\ &\quad\leqslant C\left(\sum_{V_i\ \text{continuous}}\|\bar f_i-\hat f_i\|_\infty +\sum_{V_i\ \text{categorical}}\left\|\bar f_i-\frac{\hat f_i}{\|\hat f_i\|_1}\right\|_\infty +W(P(U_1,\ldots,U_{n_U}),P(\hat U_1,\ldots,\hat U_{n_U}))\right)\\ &\quad\leqslant O\left(L_0^{-2/d_{\max}^{\text{in}}}+L_1^{-2/d_{\max}^U}+L_2^{-2/d_{\max}^U}+(\tau-\tau\log\tau)\right). \end{align*} For the second inequality, every term of the first sum has the continuous structural error bound proved here, every term of the second sum has the normalized categorical error bound proved here, and the latent term has the bound obtained using \cref{lemma:product_err}; the two sums contain only finitely many nodes. The comparison constant $C$ depends only on the fixed model, its dimensions and cardinalities, and $R$. The cubes, extensions, and networks were chosen independently of the intervention within the prescribed region. This proves the estimate uniformly throughout that region.
- why: [F2.5 reviewer] [claim-false] Cube-only minimization does not imply the claimed causal-law approximation for arbitrary selected minimizers when latent inputs lie outside the cube.

### `prop:counterexample` (`Main.tex:282-284`)

- as printed: \label{prop:counterexample} There exists a constant $c>0$ and an identifiable SCM $\mathcal{M}^*$ satisfying Assumptions \ref{assump:independence_u}-\ref{assumption:lower_bound} such that for any $\epsilon >0$, there exists an SCM $\mathcal{M}_\epsilon$ satisfying $W(P^{\mathcal{M}^*}(\boldsymbol{V}),P^{\mathcal{M}_\epsilon}(\boldsymbol{V})) \leq \epsilon $ and $|\text{ATE}_{\mathcal{M}^*} - \text{ATE}_{\mathcal{M}_\epsilon}| > c $.
- corrected: \label{prop:counterexample} There exists a constant $c>0$ and an identifiable SCM $\mathcal{M}^*$ satisfying Assumptions \ref{assump:independence_u}-\ref{assumption:lower_bound} such that for any $\epsilon >0$, there exists an SCM $\mathcal{M}_\epsilon$ satisfying $W(P^{\mathcal{M}^*}(\boldsymbol{V}),P^{\mathcal{M}_\epsilon}(\boldsymbol{V})) \leq \epsilon $ and $|\text{ATE}_{\mathcal{M}^*} - \text{ATE}_{\mathcal{M}_\epsilon}| > c $. Here, for each non-Gumbel latent law $\mathbb P$ with connected support components $C_i$, Assumption~\ref{assumption:lower_bound} is required of each normalized component law $\mathbb P|_{C_i}/\mathbb P(C_i)$, with $K=C_i$.

Assumption \ref{assump:Lip_and_bounded} explicitly identifies normalized propensity coordinates with conditional category probabilities.

### `thm:consistency` (`Main.tex:295-302`)

- as printed: \label{thm:consistency} Let $ \mathcal{M^*}$ be any SCM satisfying the assumptions of Corollary \ref{corollary:deep_nn}. Suppose that the Lipschitz constant of functions in $\mathcal{M}$ is $ L_f $, $ F:\mathbb{R}^{n_{V}}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ in (\ref{eq:opt_empiri}) is Lipschitz continuous and $\tau_n > 0 $, let $K>0$ be the constant in \cref{assump:Lip_and_bounded}, $\hat{L}_f = \sqrt{d_{\max}^{\text{in}}d_{\max}^{\text{out}}}L_f$, \begin{align*} \mathcal{F}_{0,n} &= \mathcal{NN}^{\hat{L}_{f} ,K}\left( W_{0,n} , \Theta\left(\log d^{\text{in}}_{\max}\right)\right) , \mathcal{F}_{1,n} =\mathcal{NN}^{\infty ,K}( \Theta( d^{U}_{\max}) ,L_{1,n}, \Theta( (d^{U}_{\max})^2) ,L_{2,n},\tau_n), \end{align*} where $ d_{\max}^U, d_{\max}^{\text{in}} $ and $d_{\max}^{\text{out}}$ are defined in Corollary \ref{corollary:deep_nn}, take the radius to be $\alpha_n = \epsilon_n+s_n, \epsilon_n = O(W_{0,n}^{-1/d^{\text{in}}_{\max}}+ \sum_{i=1}^2 L_{i,n}^{-2/d^U_{\max}}+ \tau _{n} \log \tau _{n}),$ $$ s_n = O(m_{n}^{-1/\left( d_{\max}^{U} +2\right)}\log m_{n} +n^{-1/{\max\{2,d_{\max}^U\}}}\log^2(n) + \log(nm_n)\lambda_n).$$ If $ m_n = \Omega(n), L_{i,n} = \Theta(m_{n}^{d_{\max}^{U} /\left( 2d_{\max}^{U} +4\right)}), i=1,2, \lim _{n\rightarrow \infty }\min\{\tau_n^{-1}, W_{0,n},(\log(nm_n)\lambda_n)^{-1}\}= \infty$ , then with probability 1, $ [\liminf _{n\rightarrow \infty } F_{n},\limsup _{n\rightarrow \infty } F_{n}] \subset [\underline{F}^{\hat{L}_f} ,F_{*}]$.
- corrected: Let $ \mathcal{M^*}$ be any SCM satisfying the assumptions of Corollary \ref{corollary:deep_nn}. Suppose that the Lipschitz constant of functions in $\mathcal{M}$ is $L_f$, $F:\mathbb{R}^{n_V}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ in (\ref{eq:opt_empiri}) is Lipschitz continuous and $\tau_n>0$, let $K>0$ be the constant in \cref{assump:Lip_and_bounded}, $\hat L_f=\sqrt{d_{\max}^{\text{in}}d_{\max}^{\text{out}}}L_f$, \begin{align*} \mathcal F_{0,n}&=\mathcal{NN}^{\hat L_f,K}\left(W_{0,n},\Theta\left(\log d_{\max}^{\text{in}}\right)\right),\qquad \mathcal F_{1,n}=\mathcal{NN}^{\infty,K}\left(\Theta(d_{\max}^U),L_{1,n},\Theta((d_{\max}^U)^2),L_{2,n},\tau_n\right), \end{align*} where $d_{\max}^U$, $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}$ and $d_{\max}^{\text{out}}$ are defined in Corollary \ref{corollary:deep_nn}. Suppose in addition that $d_{\max}^{\text{in}}\geqslant1$ and $d_{\max}^U\geqslant1$. In (\ref{eq:opt_empiri}), restrict each categorical raw structural network $q\in\mathcal F_{0,n}$ to satisfy $q(x)\in[0,\infty)^{n_i}$, $\|q(x)\|_1>0$ for every structural input $x$, and \[ \operatorname{Lip}\left(x\mapsto\frac{q(x)}{\|q(x)\|_1}\right)\leqslant\hat L_f. \] Put \[ D_U=\sum_{j=1}^{n_U}d_j^U,\qquad D=\max\{1,D_U\}, \] where the sum defining $D_U$ includes the non-Gumbel latent variables only. Take the radius to be $\alpha_n=\epsilon_n+s_n$, with positive tolerances chosen as sufficiently large constant multiples of the respective quantities in \[ \epsilon_n=O\left(W_{0,n}^{-1/d_{\max}^{\text{in}}}+\sum_{i=1}^2L_{i,n}^{-2/d_{\max}^U}+\tau_n(1-\log\tau_n)\right), \] \[ s_n=O\left(m_n^{-1/(D+2)}\log m_n+\frac{(L_{1,n}+L_{2,n})\log m_n}{\sqrt{m_n}}+n^{-1/\max\{2,D_U\}}\log^2 n+\log(nm_n)\lambda_n\right). \] For every continuous structural function $f_i$ of $\mathcal M^*$, suppose in addition that $\sup_x\|f_i(x)\|_1\leqslant K$ on its full structural input domain. Restrict every continuous structural network $\hat f_i\in\mathcal F_{0,n}$ in (\ref{eq:opt_empiri}) to satisfy this same uniform output $1$-norm bound. Retain the output bound in (\ref{eq:consistent_limiting}), namely \[ \mathcal F_L^K=\{f:\sup_x\|f(x)\|_1\leqslant K,\ \operatorname{Lip}(f)\leqslant L\}. \] Let $F_n$ be the optimal value of the empirical optimization with the objective and Sinkhorn constraint of (\ref{eq:opt_empiri}) and both the continuous and categorical restrictions just specified, and let $\underline F^{\hat L_f}$ be the optimal value of (\ref{eq:consistent_limiting}) with this bounded Lipschitz class. If $ m_n = \Omega(n), L_{i,n} = \Theta(m_{n}^{d_{\max}^{U} /\left( 2d_{\max}^{U} +4\right)}), i=1,2, \lim _{n\rightarrow \infty }\min\{\tau_n^{-1}, W_{0,n},(\log(nm_n)\lambda_n)^{-1}\}= \infty$ , then with probability 1, $ [\liminf _{n\rightarrow \infty } F_{n},\limsup _{n\rightarrow \infty } F_{n}] \subset [\underline{F}^{\hat{L}_f} ,F_{*}]$.
